records.title: Adding Tenant Profile Custom Fields (Collections Workflow)
records.fullText:
Tenant Profile Custom Fields
As you are working the delinquency and editing the custom fields on the residents profile I want you to added URL for the resident profile to the custom fields that says Profile URL.
Let me explain: every person, bill, payment, inventory item, key, work order in Appfolio has its own unique URL that you can access directly if you are logged into AppFolio. When you are on the residents profile page, copy the URL in the browser. Then go to the custom fields and click edit and paste it into the field for Tenant Profile URL.
This is going to help us a ton when making collection calls!
It only takes 10 seconds (for real) because you’re already in their profile.
Since you’re calling on every single delinquent tenant every day there’s no reason why we can’t get all of these done immediately and they should always be up to date. Eventually we will have all the residents saved. If you see this field blank in the profile- add the URL.
Also remember as you making your phone calls if someone answers and you have a conversation with them about their balance, we KNOW they live there! So while you are in the profile update the custom field for Last Known Occupancy Date. This will help us reduce the number of physical trips to the residents door to check if they live there.
records.recommendation:
## Purpose
This policy establishes the requirement for leasing and collections staff to populate two custom fields — **Tenant Profile URL** and **Last Known Occupancy Date** — on every resident profile in AppFolio.

## Background
Every resident, bill, payment, inventory item, key, and work order in AppFolio has a unique URL that can be accessed directly by anyone logged into AppFolio. Capturing this URL on the resident's profile allows staff to navigate directly to a resident's record without searching, which meaningfully speeds up the collections process.

## Procedure
1. **Locate the Profile URL.** While viewing a resident's profile page in AppFolio, copy the URL from the browser's address bar.
2. **Update the Custom Field.** Navigate to the resident's custom fields, select Edit, and paste the copied URL into the field labeled "Tenant Profile URL."
3. **Update During Delinquency Calls.** Any time a staff member works a delinquent account and finds a blank Tenant Profile URL field, the field must be completed immediately.
4. **Record Last Known Occupancy.** If a staff member speaks with a resident by phone regarding their balance, this confirms the resident currently occupies the unit. The staff member must update the "Last Known Occupancy Date" custom field accordingly. This reduces the need for physical trips to confirm occupancy.

## Responsibility
All staff working delinquent accounts are responsible for ensuring both custom fields are completed and current for every resident profile they access.

records.title: Following Up with Leads: Timing & Methods
records.fullText:
Follow Up Methods
Effective follow-up in property management leasing involves contacting prospective tenants promptly and regularly after they show interest in a property. This can be achieved through phone calls, emails, and even personalized tours or video messages. Timing is key, with a quick response (within 5-10 minutes of a lead contacting you) being crucial for securing a lease.
Here’s a more detailed breakdown of effective follow-up methods:
Prompt Contact:
Initial Contact:
Respond to inquiries via phone call within the first 5 minutes of a lead contacting you. This demonstrates professionalism and eagerness to help. A phone call provides a more personal touch and allows for direct communication, especially when answering questions or scheduling a tour.
Follow-Up First 24 Hours:
If attempting to make contact via phone is unsuccessful, send a follow-up email and text message. Three (3) follow up attempts within the first 24 hours are required by switching up the touch points (call/email/text).
Follow-Up After 24 Hours (Day 2 - 4):
If the prospect has not responded to calls, email, and text messages, within the first 24 hours, continue to follow up via phone/email/text message once per day for the next 3 days.
Follow-Up After Day 4:
Send valuable information, property updates, and personalized messages via email and text once per week.

records.title: Personalizing Lead Follow-Up
records.fullText:
Personalize Follow Up
Personalizing your follow-up communication adds a human touch, making the lead feel valued and understood. It moves beyond the transactional nature of the business and builds a relationship based on trust and empathy. Personalizing follow-up involves tailoring communication to individual prospect needs and preferences. This can be achieved utilizing the following items listed below.
Personalize Your Message:
Address them by name:
Use their first name to make the communication feel more personal and less transactional.
Reference their specific situation:
If they mentioned a specific property, neighborhood, or need, tailor your message to address that.
Leverage video messages:
Consider sending a personalized video message instead of just a text or email. A video gives a human touch and allows leads to see your face, which can create a stronger connection.
Leverage customized memes :
Consider sending personalized memes relative to their specific interests and preferences.
Tailor your language:
Use language that resonates with their specific interests and preferences.
Example:
“Hello [Prospect’s Name], I hope you’re enjoying the Austin summer weather. As we discussed, I wanted to share some local resources about [specific neighborhood] and [specific amenity] that might be helpful to you”.
Offer Clear Next Steps:
Make it easy to take action:
Clearly outline the next steps they can take, such as scheduling a tour, calling you, or visiting your website.
Example:
“If you’d like to schedule a tour, please reply to this email or call me at [phone number]. I’m happy to answer any further questions you may have”.
Maintain a Professional and Respectful Tone:
Be polite and courteous:
Address the prospect respectfully and maintain a professional tone throughout your communication.
Listen to their needs:
Pay attention to their questions and concerns and address them accordingly.
Be helpful and informative:
Offer useful information about the properties you manage and the neighborhood where they’re interested in living.

records.title: Setting Occupancy Standards
records.fullText:
Metric Property Management: Occupancy Standards
Occupancy Standards Policy
Purpose To establish and communicate occupancy limits for all rental units and outline the process for addressing over-occupancy situations in compliance with Fair Housing laws and local ordinances.
Occupancy Standard
We follow the “two (2) persons per bedroom + 1 additional occupant” rule:
Infants under 24 months of age are not counted toward the total.
This applies to all residents regardless of relationship, unless stricter local, state, or federal occupancy limits apply.

During the Leasing Process
Leasing staff must verify intended occupancy before approving applications.
Never ask a prospect of applicant how many adults or how many children. Always ask “how many people will be living in the apartment.” Asking how many adults or how many children may open up the company to a Fair Housing complaint related to familial status.
Legal Adults over the age of 18 must be listed as lease holders except for
Full time live in caretakevers (occupants)
Persons over the age of 18 that are under the legal guardianship of another adult in the household (occupant)
All occupants must be listed on the lease agreement.
Commissions will not be paid on any lease over the approved occupancy limit at move-in.
If Over-Occupancy is Found During the Lease Term
Document the situation in detail (names of occupants, relationship, dates observed, any communication).
Notify the Property Manager immediately for review.
Provide the resident with written notice that they are in violation of the lease occupancy terms.
Give the resident 10 days to correct the violation.
If space allows, and management approves, offer the resident the option to transfer to a larger unit that meets occupancy standards.
Standard transfer fees will apply, including any applicable rent difference, deposit adjustments, and administrative fees.
If unresolved and no transfer is accepted, proceed with enforcement up to and including lease termination in accordance with local laws.
At the End of the Lease Term
If over-occupancy is confirmed at renewal time:
Renewal will not be offered unless occupancy is brought into compliance.
Non-renewal will be offered unless occupancy is brought into compliance.
The resident may be offered the option to transfer to a larger unit with transfer fees applying, provided the resident(s) qualify and rental history is positive.
All decisions must be documented in the resident file.
Fair Housing Compliance
This policy will be applied equally and consistently to all applicants and residents, without discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, disability, secual orientation, familial status, or national origin.
Quick Reference for Leasing Staff

Commission Rule: No leasing commission is payable for over-occupancy units.

records.title: Overcoming Leasing Objections
records.fullText:
Overcoming Objections
Author and speaker Bo Bennett once said, “An objection is not a rejection; it is simply a request for more information.”
5 Steps for Handling Any Objections
Step 1: Listen and Empathize
As a leasing agent, handling objections effectively begins with the capacity to listen attentively and empathize genuinely. By actively listening — paying attention to spoken and unspoken messages — and comprehending the potential residents’ concerns, you demonstrate that you hear, understand, and value their perspective.
Empathizing helps build rapport and puts the person at ease as you work together to find a resolution. By embracing this critical first step, you can create a positive environment for open and honest communication. Most people simply want to feel heard and understood, so any chance you have in winning a lease starts here.
Step 2: Ask Questions and Clarify
To effectively overcome an objection, leasing agents must learn to ask insightful questions and seek clarification; both play a pivotal role in uncovering the root cause behind a prospect’s objection.
The goal is not merely to gather information but to discover the underlying concerns that may not be immediately apparent. By posing thought-provoking questions, you can encourage the prospect to articulate their objections more clearly, providing you with valuable insight into their mindset and preferences.
These questions should be strategic and catered to elicit detailed responses that shed light on the true nature of the objection. This step creates a platform for meaningful dialogue, enabling you to address objections more effectively and tailor your solutions to resonate with the person’s specific needs and concerns.
Step 3: Rephrase the Objection
As a leasing agent for apartments, “rephrasing the objection” is a crucial step in the objection-handling process. It involves more than merely parroting back the client’s concern — it entails actively listening, interpreting, and reflecting on the objection in a way that showcases your understanding and empathy. By repeating the objection in your own words, you demonstrate that you have grasped the core of their apprehension and desire to address it effectively.
This step serves multiple purposes. By rephrasing the objection, you:
- Validate the resident or prospect’s perspective
- Ensure mutual clarity on the issue at hand
- Show your commitment to resolving their concerns. 
Rephrasing the objection acts as a bridge of communication, enhancing the connection between you and the prospect by affirming you are on the same page and ready to collaborate on finding a suitable solution.
Through this process, you reaffirm their trust in your ability to navigate objections skillfully and provide tailored resolutions that align with their needs.
Step 4: Offer Solutions
To offer a solution involves presenting tailored and practical resolutions to effectively address objections, and for leasing agents, this is a pivotal phase in the objection-handling process.
By leveraging your expertise and understanding of the prospect’s concerns, you can offer personalized solutions demonstrating your commitment to meeting their needs. Whether it involves proposing alternative options, outlining specific benefits, or providing additional information, the aim is to alleviate concerns and showcase your proactive approach to problem-solving.
This step not only serves to overcome objections but also illustrates your dedication to fostering a positive and collaborative relationship, ultimately paving the way for successful resolution and agreement.
Step 5: Check for Agreement
It can be tempting to stop at Step 4, believing that the hurdle is cleared once you have provided a viable solution. However, a critical step in the objection-handling process is to check for agreement. After presenting a solution, ensuring that the prospect genuinely agrees with the proposed resolution is essential. This involves actively seeking feedback and allowing time to express any lingering concerns or reservations.
You can address any hesitations and refine the solution if needed by engaging in open dialogue and encouraging prospects to voice their thoughts. Additionally, by offering research, you convey dedication to going the extra mile to find the most suitable resolution.
This step reinforces the collaborative nature of the resident-agent relationship. It signifies your commitment to ensuring the people who live in your community are not just satisfied, but genuinely enthusiastic about the proposed solution.
Ultimately, checking for agreement strengthens the sense of partnership and trust, laying the groundwork for a successful outcome and a positive overall experience.
Top 10 Objections and Potential Solutions:
Objection #1: “I’m just not sure I can afford the rent.”
Solution: How you respond will differ based on the person or circumstance, but here are some ideas for overcoming this objection with residents and prospects.
- **For a prospective resident**, you could check for similar apartments, smaller apartments, a longer lease term, etc. 
Objection #2: “There are brand new apartments within a mile, and they are only $60 more per month.”
Solution: If you work at a property in a growing metropolitan area, be prepared to overcome this objection.
Here are a few questions to ask:
- “What is the most important thing about finding an apartment: amenities, location, or having a brand-new apartment?”
- “Have you asked, or considered, what rent increases might take effect once it is time to renew?”
The lease-up phase involves reasonable rates to fill a property, but rates typically increase dramatically when the lease is up for renewal.
Objection #3: “There is no washer/dryer in my apartment?”
Solution: Based on the situation, below are some suggestions.
No washer/dryer in the apartment:
- If applicable, remind the prospect the property has a laundry room, which will save them time by being able to wash multiply loads at once.
- If washer/dryer hookups are available in the unit, suggest a rent-to-own option. If this is a common issue for your community, research local rent-to-own stores that offer this so you can provide that information. 
Objection #4: “I’ve read your reviews online, and quite frankly, I’m a little worried.”
Solution: First and foremost, you should be aware of any negative comments posted about your property online. More importantly, you should actively address them. If not, then you unfortunately have a reputation management issue, and you need a solution to address it.
In the ever-growing world of social media and online review sites, being proactive with comments and reviews is paramount. And if you’re only hearing negative reviews from prospective residents, that’s a problem. However, here are a few leasing agent tips to keep in mind:
Be positive and professional: Always remember to respond to negative reviews positively and professionally. This will show your prospects you are attempting to resolve any issues with current residents.
Acknowledge their concern. Assure them that the leasing staff investigates any situations and will do everything within their power to make it right as customer service is a top priority.
Invite them to an event: Sometimes seeing is believing, so invite prospective residents to attend your next resident event.
Objection #5: “These [insert the concern: carpets, appliances, cabinets, etc.] are old and really need to be replaced.”
Solution: Based on the concern, below are some suggestions.
Carpet: If there is a plan for carpet replacement, let them know it’s a project on the horizon. Instead of focusing on the carpet, help turn the prospect’s attention to the other positive features of the apartment (e.g., spacious layout, updated kitchen, great location. If possible, show them photos of how others have added throw rugs to improve the look and feel.
Appliances: This might be an opportunity to highlight your maintenance program, assuring prospective residents that your teams promptly address necessary repairs. Again, play to the positives, whatever those might be.
Cabinets: If the cabinets need replacement, do you have options for residents to make improvements? If they can’t be replaced, could you offer to have them painted? Are there rent-friendly hardware options you could suggest? Providing examples and photos is always helpful, if possible.
Objection #6: “I really need to discuss this with my partner (husband, roommate, etc.).”
Solution: According to a recent study by Harvard’s Joint Center for Housing Studies, “rental prices are unaffordable for a record number of Americans with half of all renters paying more than 30% of their income on rent and utilities.” So, it’s important to acknowledge that it is a big decision. But before they disconnect the call, here are some options:
Ask them, “If you were the only person deciding on the apartment, would you want to make a deposit?”
Offer a 24-hour hold for the apartment.
Objection #7: “The living room (or kitchen or bedroom) is just too small. My furniture won’t fit.”
Solution: Your best tool to overcome this simple objection is to offer the measurements of the room. Beds and sofas tend to take up the most real estate in an apartment layout, so keep in mind the most common size of furniture items:
Regular three-seat sofas typically measure about 35 inches deep by 84 inches wide.
Loveseats often measure 60 inches wide by 35 inches deep
Apartment-size sofas are usually between 68 and 80 inches wide, with a few inches shaved off to save space in depth.

Based on their furniture, you can provide them with the measurements and the amount of space a bed or other piece of furniture would take up in any of the rooms. If space is a hurdle you can’t overcome, consider referring them to a different Metric property.
Objection #8: “I’m not really sure about the neighborhood.”
Solution: Know the neighborhood so you can speak truthfully to the area. More importantly, you need to know every positive piece of information about your neighborhood; to do that, you must take some time to explore the area.
Highlight Neighborhood Benefits:
Positive attributes: Emphasize the neighborhood’s strengths, such as proximity to public transportation, schools, parks, or shopping centers.
Crime Statistics: If safety is a primary concern, discuss the neighborhood’s crime rate, police presence, and any community watch programs. If available, provide accurate crime statistics for the area to address safety concerns.
Safety measures: If the property has security features like gated access, surveillance cameras, or onsite staff, highlight these.
Share your experiences: If you live in the neighborhood or have personal knowledge, share positive experiences.
Testimonials from current residents: Ask if you can share testimonials from satisfied residents with similar concerns.
Knowledge is power. Be clear about what your community offers, and then back that up with facts you can share.
Objection #9: “I’m just not ready yet. This is only the first apartment community I’ve toured.”
Solution: In this case, utilize the 24-hour hold. Also, ask the prospect about the other communities they plan to tour; it will give you an idea of your competition if they are willing to share that information.
Objection #10: “[Insert name of your competition] is running a special of no deposit down and one month free. Do you have any specials?”
Solution: This one is a bit trickier to deal with, but it’s equally crucial for you to know your competition. Pay attention to lease specials and promotions to be prepared and proactive in overcoming this hurdle. As you become aware of the competitor specials being offered, ask your manager what you can do to balance this out.
If your community doesn’t have a specific first-time lease special, offer alternative incentives that might appeal to prospective residents. This could include:
Concessions: Rent credits, waived fees, or discounted utilities.
Upgrades: Offering upgrades like upgraded flooring or appliances.
Special promotions: For example, a “refer a friend” program or a loyalty program.
Focus on the overall value: Emphasize that your community offers long-term value beyond short-term promotions. Discuss factors like property management, community events, and the overall living experience.
Avoid focusing solely on price: While price is important, show how your community’s value proposition extends beyond the initial rental cost.
By acknowledging the competition, offering alternative incentives, emphasizing long-term value, and providing a personalized experience, you can effectively overcome the “lease specials” objection and increase your chances of securing a lease.
Leasing Agent Tips: Let “Ideas” Be Your Guide
An acrostic mnemonic is a sentence or poem where each part of the text’s first letter (or letters) represents something you’re trying to memorize. It’s a valuable tool to help remember things.
While you likely are familiar with some familiar mnemonics — colors of the rainbow: ROY G BIV or the order of operations in math: Please Excuse My Dear Aunt Sally — here’s one to help leasing agents for apartments.
“IDEAS” is a common acrostic used in the real estate industry, particularly in apartment leasing, and it’s a helpful tool for identifying and addressing objections from prospective residents.
Here’s a breakdown of each letter:
I: Identify the Real Objection
Understanding the underlying reason for the objection is crucial for providing a relevant and effective response.
D: Discover Your Competition
Knowing what other properties offer can help you position your community more competitively.
E: Explore Your Sister Communities
If applicable, consider leveraging the strengths of other properties within your management company or portfolio.
A: Analyze Your Brand Advantages
Highlight the unique features and benefits that set your community apart from the competition.
S: Suggest Solutions
Offer tailored solutions that address prospective residents’ concerns and meet their needs.
This acrostic provides a structured approach to handling objections and increases the likelihood of securing a lease.

records.title: Syncing Knock Calendar with Outlook
records.fullText:
Knock: Sync Knock Outlook
Resolution
Step 1:
On the Calendar page of your Knock account click the Sync button:

Next to Outlook, click Connect:

Step 2:
In the modal window that pops up, click Copy next to the calendar URL:

Step 3:
A. Outlook desktop (most common)
At the top of Outlook, click Open Calendar (sometimes shows as New Calendar) and then select From Internet… in the dropdown.
Now right click and Paste the Knock calendar link into the field. Then click OK.
If you don’t have any Knock appointments yet, Outlook will tell you so. Click Yes.
Do you want to subscribe to calendar? Click Yes.
Now you are done! To have the two calendars overlap (as opposed to side by side), click the little left-pointing arrow on the Knock calendar:
Now all of your Knock appointments will appear in Outlook! Note that Outlook only allows for one-way syncing- i.e. anything you add in Outlook will NOT appear in Knock. So you want to add all your tours into Knock as well as any busy times you don’t want renters to book.
B. Outlook.com (365)
Go to your 365 calendar on Outlook.com. At the top of the screen, click Add Calendar.
Then right click and Paste in the URL you copied. Give your calendar a name Save.
C. Outlook.com (regular)
At the top of the screen, click Import.
On the left-hand side of the screen that pops up, click Subscribe and then right-click and Paste the URL that you copied from Knock into the “Calendar URL” field.
Name the calendar Knock (or whatever you want!) and click Subscribe.
And that’s it! Now all of your appointments in Knock will push to Outlook every 15 minutes (but not vice versa) :)
records.recommendation:
## Purpose
This procedure explains how to sync a Knock calendar with Outlook so that scheduled tours and appointments appear on both calendars.

## Important Note
Outlook allows one-way syncing only. Appointments created in Knock will appear in Outlook; appointments created directly in Outlook will not appear in Knock. All tours and blocked/unavailable times must be entered in Knock so that renters cannot book over them.

## Procedure

### Step 1: Copy the Knock Calendar Link
1. On the Calendar page of the Knock account, select **Sync**.
2. Next to Outlook, select **Connect**.
3. In the window that appears, select **Copy** next to the calendar URL.

### Step 2: Connect the Calendar in Outlook

**Option A — Outlook Desktop (most common)**
1. At the top of Outlook, select **Open Calendar** (or **New Calendar**), then select **From Internet...**.
2. Paste the Knock calendar link into the field and select **OK**.
3. If prompted with "Do you want to subscribe to calendar?", select **Yes**.
4. To overlay the Knock calendar on the primary calendar instead of viewing them side by side, select the left-pointing arrow on the Knock calendar.

**Option B — Outlook.com (365)**
1. On the Outlook.com 365 calendar, select **Add Calendar**.
2. Paste the copied URL, name the calendar, and select **Save**.

**Option C — Outlook.com (Regular)**
1. At the top of the screen, select **Import**.
2. Select **Subscribe**, then paste the copied URL into the Calendar URL field.
3. Name the calendar and select **Subscribe**.

## Result
Once connected, all Knock appointments will sync to Outlook approximately every 15 minutes.

records.title: Initiating Move-Outs Immediately in AppFolio
records.fullText:
Immediate Initiation of Move-Out Process in AppFolio

Purpose
This SOP establishes the required procedure for initiating the move‑out process in AppFolio immediately upon receiving any indication that a resident has vacated their apartment. The goal is to maintain accurate records, ensure timely processing, and prevent compliance issues resulting from delayed move‑out actions.

Scope
This policy applies to all leasing agents, property managers, assistant managers, and any staff responsible for resident communication, resident profile maintenance, and AppFolio property management functions.

Policy Statement
Residents who confirm, indicate, or imply that they have vacated their unit for any reason must be processed as move‑outs immediately in AppFolio. Under no circumstances should a resident who has left the premises remain in a status such as Current, Notice, or Eviction if it is known they have vacated.

Procedure
1. Resident Notification of Vacating
If a resident indicates—verbally, via email, text, voicemail, portal message, or through a third party—that they have vacated their apartment:
1.1. The move‑out process must be initiated immediately in AppFolio.
Do not wait to confirm through an inspection or walkthrough.
Initiation of the move‑out process is required even if additional steps (keys return, walkthrough scheduling, final ledger work, etc.) still need to be completed.

2. Do Not Delay Move‑Out Due to Time Constraints
2.1. Staff must not postpone initiating the move‑out due to workload, unavailable time to walk the unit, or pending documentation.
2.2. The physical walk‑through and final account processing may follow, but the move‑out status in AppFolio must be created immediately.

3. Prohibited Notations in Resident Profiles
3.1. There must never be delinquency notes, resident profile notes, or account comments that state or imply:
“Resident skipped,”
“Resident moved out,”
“Unit appears vacant,”
while the resident’s status remains Current, Notice, or Eviction.
3.2. These notations indicate knowledge of a move‑out, which mandates immediate initiation of the move‑out process.
Leaving the resident in an incorrect status is non‑compliant.

4. Compliance and Accountability
4.1. All agents and staff are responsible for taking immediate action when informed of a resident vacating.
4.2. Failure to initiate the move‑out process upon knowledge of a skip or confirmed vacancy will result in review and accountability measures.
4.3. Routine audits will be performed to identify:
Delays in move‑out initiation
Improper resident statuses
Notes indicating a skip or move‑out without corresponding move‑out action
Any agent found to be non‑compliant will be held responsible according to company policy.

5. Documentation Requirements
5.1. Once move‑out is initiated, staff must ensure the following documentation is added as available:
Resident’s communication indicating they vacated
Photos or videos (if applicable) after walk‑through
Any relevant correspondence or notices
5.2. Documentation should be completed promptly, but only after the move‑out has been started.

6. Quality Assurance
6.1. Supervisors will monitor AppFolio activity to verify timely and accurate move‑out processing.
6.2. Any discrepancies will be addressed immediately to prevent financial, operational, and legal complications.

Summary of Key Requirements
Start the move‑out in AppFolio immediately once you learn a resident has vacated.
Do not delay due to time limitations or pending inspections.
Never leave notes stating a resident has skipped or moved out while keeping them in an active status.
Compliance is mandatory and will be enforced through ongoing audits.

VA Invoice Processing Policy (Accounting & Asana Workflow)
Overview
This policy outlines the standard process for handling Virtual Assistant (VA) invoices, from task creation in Asana through invoice entry, approval, and payment in AppFolio. The goal is to ensure consistency, accuracy, and proper documentation across accounting and operations.
This process applies to all VA invoices and must be followed without exception.

Key Principles
Every VA invoice must have a corresponding Asana task
All VA invoices are entered in AppFolio as Metric corporate expenses
All VAs should be setup as vendors in AppFolio
The Asana task serves as the source of truth for invoice tracking
Tasks must be completed only after payment are finished and are entered in Appfolio

Asana Task Requirements
Step 1: Create the VA Invoice Task in Asana: Task Creation
Each VA invoice must be represented by one Asana task.
The task must include:
VA name
Invoice period
Invoice amount
The VA’s invoice attached (PDF or image)
This task represents a single invoice only.

Automatic Task Routing
Once created, the VA invoice task must:
Automatically copy into the Daily Accounting project under “Invoice Processing” section
The asana task is automatically assigned to Dave Flores
This ensures accounting visibility and ownership without manual follow-up.

Payment Method
Each VA invoice task must include a field labeled Payment Method.
The Lead VA responsible for processing the payment must select the payment method used to pay the invoice.
Available options include:
Wise
Remitly
Wire Transfer
Other approved VA payment method
This field must be selected before the task is considered ready for processing.

After the Asana task has been marked as Approved and Paid, the task will be routed and assigned to Dave Flores for invoice processing.



Step 2: Entering the Bill: AppFolio Invoice Processing
Accounting must enter the VA invoice in AppFolio using the same process as any other Metric corporate expense.
Steps:
Confirm the VA is set up as a vendor in AppFolio

- If the VA is not already listed, create the VA as a vendor in AppFolio before proceeding.

Step 3: Approve the Invoice: Approval & Payment

Current Payment Account:

All current VA payment methods (including Wise, Remitly, and wire transfers) are tied to this account.

Step 4: Closing the Asana Task
Once the following are complete:

👉 The Asana task must be marked COMPLETE.
No task should be closed before all AppFolio steps are finalized.

This policy will be updated once the transition is approved and active.

Compliance

records.fullText:
Metric will complete replacement reserve draw requests upon request or on an agreed schedule for properties. Generally this cadence is agreed when the property comes on board or the loan is started.

- It is critical that replacement reserve draw schedule and rules (draw eligible items) are communicated in advance so Metric can account for the draw items in a manner where they can easily track the items. 

Request periodic replacement reserve draws by emailing the Regional Manager and Property Accountant with the date the replacement reserve draw is needed and any specific information related to the draw, such as goal amount or urgency of the draw.

Metric cannot work on replacement reserve draws whatsoever from the 5th of the month to the 17th of the month due to the schedule for monthly bank reconciliations and financial packages.

The ideal time for Metric to complete replacement reserve draws is from the 17th to the 25th of the month. If a client prefers a _quick_ turn around on a replacement reserve draw they should schedule it during this time.

**✅ Step-by-Step Procedure: Auditing After-Hours Work Orders**

**1. Access the Audit List**

- Navigate to the [After Hours NOT Marked Work Orders](https://metricpropertymanagement.appfolio.com/buffered_reports/277) link in AppFolio.
- This is a **daily recurring task**, typically done by end-of-day.

**2. Identify Work Orders**

- Review work orders marked as **“Work Done”**.
- Focus on those with **start times beyond 6:00 PM**, which may qualify as after-hours.
- This report is formatted to pull ALL work orders NOT marked after hours intentionally but the room for error is the work MAY actually be after hours and the tech just did not click the after hours button- this is what you are looking for.

**3. Verify Time Logs**

- Open each work order and check:
    - **Start and end times**.
    - **Action logs** for tech activity to confirm or dispute if the work is after hours.

**4. Confirm Validity**

- Cross-check with the **maintenance group chat** or technician communication if needed.
- Ensure technicians have sent **proof of presence** at the property (e.g., photos with timestamps).

**5. Determine Rate Eligibility**

- If verified as after-hours:
    - Proceed with billing at **after-hours rate (already set in Smart Maintenance)**
- If **not verified**:
    - During billing, **unclick the “After Hours” option**.
    - Revert to **regular rate.**

**6. Billing Process**

- Click **“Mark Ready to Bill”**.
- Then click **“Create Bill”**.
- Adjust the **rate** based on verification (not the time).
- Finalize the bill with correct charges.

**7. Handle Discrepancies**

- If a technician incorrectly marks a work order as after-hours:
    - Send a **reminder** (no formal sanction).
    - General notices are issued to discourage misuse.

## Purpose

This guide outlines the process for contacting Austin Energy to activate electricity service for a vacant unit at a manage property by Metric (example Sunset Palms).

---

# Austin Energy Contact Information

**Phone Number:** **512-494-9400**

When prompted:

1. Select **Residential** from the phone menu.
1. Wait to be connected with a customer service representative.

---

# Activation Process

### Step 1: Introduce the Call

Once connected, say:

"Hello, I'm calling to activate an electricity account for one of our apartment units at Sunset Palms."

The representative will then ask for the property information.

---

### Step 2: Provide the Property Information

Provide:

- Property Name: **Sunset Palms**
- Property Address
- Unit Number requiring activation

The representative may ask you to confirm the address again. Simply repeat:

- Complete property address
- Unit number

---

### Step 3: Provide the Tax Identification Number (EIN)

The representative will request the business Tax ID (EIN).

To locate it:

1. Open **AppFolio**.
1. Search for **Sunset Palms**.
1. Open the property.
1. Click the **Owner**.
1. Confirm the owner is:

**Greystone Bridge Loan Sub REIT Inc**

[IMAGE]

1. Scroll down to the **Attachments** section.
1. Open the **W-9** attachment.
1. Locate the **Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN/EIN)**.

[IMAGE]

1. Provide the EIN to the representative.

[IMAGE]

[IMAGE]

### Step 4: Provide the Business Name

The representative will also request the legal business name.

You can find this on the same **W-9** document.

Look for **Item #2**.

Provide:

[IMAGE]

**Graystone Bridge Waterloo Austin LLC**

---

### Step 5: Provide the Contact Number

If asked for the best contact number, provide the main office line:

**Main Contact Number:**

**512-817-0390**

If the representative requests an **on-site contact number**:

- Reach out to K**ara** to determine the appropriate onsite contact.
- If Kara is unavailable, provide **Kara's phone number**.

---

# Technician Visit

The representative will provide the scheduled activation date.

### Important Notes

- Activation is **typically scheduled for the next business day**, depending on technician availability.
- **Austin Energy does not provide a specific arrival time.**
- The technician may call before arriving.

**Ensure someone is available to answer incoming calls** so the technician can complete the activation without delay.

---

# Before Ending the Call

Before disconnecting, make sure to obtain the following:

- ✅ Austin Energy Account Number
- ✅ Scheduled activation date
- ✅ Any additional instructions provided by the representative

Document all details immediately after the call.

---

# Post-Call Actions

After completing the activation:

1. Record the **Austin Energy account number**.
1. Document the scheduled technician visit date.
1. Write a brief summary of the conversation.
1. Notify the appropriate team members (such as Cara) of the scheduled activation.
1. Ensure the contact phone remains available on the scheduled activation day in case the technician calls.

---

# Quick Reference

| Item | Information |
| --- | --- |
| Utility Provider | Austin Energy |
| Phone Number | **512-494-9400** |
| Phone Menu | Select **Residential** |
| Property | Sunset Palms |
| Owner in AppFolio | Graystone Bridge Loan Subret Incorporated |
| Business Name (W-9 Item #2) | Graystone Bridge Waterloo Austin LLC |
| Main Contact Number | **512-817-0390** |
| EIN | Located in the property's **W-9 attachment** in AppFolio |
| Technician Arrival | No specific arrival time provided; keep phone lines available |
| After Call | Record account number, activation date, and conversation summary |

Completed a live activation call with Austin Energy for Sunset Palms units 207, 213, 214, and 216. A few corrections/additions for future reference:

1. IMPORTANT CORRECTION — EIN vs. TIN: Austin Energy's system did NOT match the number labeled "Taxpayer Identification Number" on the W-9 (99-3889845). They specifically need the Federal Employer Identification Number (EIN), which for this property is: EIN: 99-4982530 (This number was located in separate client documentation, not on the W-9 itself. records.fullText:
Emergency Management & Maintenance Request Policy

**Purpose**

Safeguard resident wellbeing, preserve property value, and ensure clear accountability in both standard and emergency maintenance situations.

**1) Service Intake & Channels (How Residents Should Request Service)**

**Resident options**

- **AppFolio**: Submit an online service request. 
- **Maintenance Hotline (737) 5204891**: Third-party call center; **English & Spanish** support. 

**What happens after submission**

- The request is **logged in AppFolio** (visible for resident tracking). 
- It is **auto assigned** to the appropriate technician. 
- The assigned tech receives a **text/call** with request details. 

**If residents email or message staff**

- Staff must **direct residents** to AppFolio or the Hotline. 
- **Do not** submit a request **on a resident’s behalf**. Requests entered internally **do not auto assign to on call** and create risk of delay. 
- **Internal service requests (general property items only):** 
- These are **entered only by Jaen or the Maintenance Coordinator (Maria)**, who own tracking and action. 
- If you believe a general property item needs an internal work order, **message Maria and Jaen** with details; they will enter and assign it. 
- **Exception (rare):** If **Jaen explicitly instructs** you to capture a general property item, assign it to **Maria and Jaen** (and only as directed by Jaen). 

**2) What Counts as an Emergency**

Residents must select **“Urgent”** in AppFolio for emergencies. Staff should verify the situation **matches the list below or reasonably presents an urgent health/safety risk**.

**Examples (not exhaustive):**

- **Active flooding or burst pipes**, or water that **cannot be contained**. 
- **Gas leaks or gas odors**. 
- **Complete loss of power** to the **apartment/room** or to **essential appliances** (e.g., **refrigerator, stove**). 
- **Fire or fire hazards** (including smoke or burning smells). 
- **Security risks** (e.g., broken doors/windows; **cannot secure** the apartment). 
- **Sewer backups** or **water contamination** within or outside the unit. 
- **Lockouts**. 
- **Nonfunctional toilet in a one-bathroom unit**. 
- **Major roof leaks**. 
- Loss of major utilities: **electric, gas, water, sewer, drainage**. 
- **No AC when outside temperature is > 85°F** or **no heat when < 65°F**. 
- Any condition that presents an **immediate health or safety concern**. 

**Misuse of emergency channels**

Residents who misuse the emergency process may receive targeted education on proper use. Staff should verify whether the request meets the standard above or **reasonably** appears urgent.

**3) Immediate Actions When You Receive an Emergency Report**

**Onsite (during business hours or after hours)**

1. **Assist the resident in calling the emergency line immediately.** Ensure they are able to complete the call. 
1. If a request must be logged urgently due to system issues, **message your team lead**, then contact **Maria and Jaen** for direction. 
1. **An approver (Maria/Jaen)** will **create and assign** the work order for you to handle immediately or for reassignment, depending on the situation. 
1. **Never** enter an emergency as an **internal** service request; internal entries do **not** route to on call. 

**Afterhours, in person**

- Help the resident call the emergency line. **Do not** enter the request manually. 
- If the issue is clearly urgent, **message your team lead, Maria, and Jaen** for approval/assignment. 

**Backup escalation (availability failover)**

- If the **Maintenance Coordinator (Maria)** is unavailable for **> 15 minutes** during an emergency, escalate to **Jaen**, then to **Bekah (Rebekah)**. 

**4) OnCall & Coverage Standards**

- For emergency calls, technicians are expected to be **onsite within 1 hour** of the call being received; **never more than 2 hours**. 
- **On call techs must be sober and fully available** for the entire on call period. 
- **On call shifts may not be traded** unless **approved by the Property Manager** and updated in the **OnCall Calendar**. 
- If the assigned tech is overwhelmed, **immediately escalate to your supervisor** and request help; lack of availability is **not** an acceptable reason for delay. Ensure you have coverage. 

**5) Access & Documentation Requirements (Do Not Leave Life/Safety Issues Unresolved)**

**Required documentation for every emergency work order**

- **Arrival & departure times**. 
- **Location photos** (as applicable). 
- **Description of the issue encountered**. 
- **Steps taken** to resolve or contain. 
- **Photos** supporting the work performed (as applicable). 
- **Escalation notes** if any portion remains unresolved. _We do not leave life/safety issues without escalating to supervisors to confirm next steps._ 

**Leasing team actions (when escalation is needed on an already entered urgent item)**

- Add a **note** on the work order. 
- **Escalate in the Urgent Work Order group chat**. 
- If no timely response, **escalate to Jaen** in the same chat. 

**Access & entry during an active emergency**

- Technicians must **enter the unit** to address an active emergency. 
- If **resident keys do not work** and the resident **cannot be reached** after multiple contact attempts (**calls/texts**), **drill the lock** to prevent further property damage. 
- **During business hours:** contact **Maria** for coordination and next steps. 
- **After hours:** escalate to **Jaen**, then **Bekah**, for coordination and to ensure clear **communication to the resident** and proper **key handling**. 
- **Immediately escalate** to your supervisor when a lock is drilled. Coordinate returning **or delivering a key to the resident**; do not leave the situation without a plan for secure access. 

**6) Vendor Escalation (Outside Team Scope)**

- If the issue exceeds the maintenance team’s scope: **escalate to Jaen**. 
- If **Jaen** is unavailable, escalate to **Bekah**. 
- The appropriate **licensed vendor** will be facilitated and dispatched as needed. Document all vendor actions in the work order. 

**7) Emergency Surge Protocol**

- During high-volume events (**including inclement weather**), non-on call staff may be asked to assist. 
- All team members are expected to help. **These are people’s homes—act with urgency and compassion.** 

**8) Accountability & Discipline**

- Because emergencies directly impact **resident life and safety**, policy violations carry **severe consequences**: 
- **Written disciplinary action and/or suspension** (at minimum). 
- Up to **immediate termination**, depending on seriousness. 
- Failing to escalate or respond appropriately can result in **legal liability** and serious **life/safety risks**. When in doubt, **over escalate and learn**, rather than under escalate and leave residents in dangerous conditions. 

**9) After-hours Materials, Purchasing & Resident Safety**

**Purchasing authority after hours**

- When emergency resolution requires **materials/tools not on hand after hours**, obtain approval to purchase. **After-hours payments can be made by Jaen or Bekah.** 
- Document approval in the work order (**approver name, time, amount/limit**) and attach a photo of the **receipt** by the next business day. Follow the company purchasing card or approved reimbursement process as directed. 

**If stores are closed until morning**

- **Do not leave residents unsafe.** Before deferring work until opening hours, **exhaust all reasonable avenues** to mitigate the issue: 
- Check **on hand inventory**, neighboring community stock, on call supply bins, and any **24hour suppliers**. 
- Consider dispatching a **licensed vendor** if delay creates a life/safety risk or substantial property damage; escalate to **Jaen** (then **Bekah** if Jaen is unavailable). 
- If true deferral is unavoidable, **leave the unit in the safest condition possible**, which may include: 
- Shutting off water at the **fixture** and/or **unit main**; installing temporary caps/containment; placing **warning signage**. 
- Isolating **electrical hazards**; securing doors/windows/locks; providing **temporary mitigation** (e.g., portable AC/heat, temporary lock hardware) pending approval. 
- Communicating an **ETA** for permanent repair and the **return visit time**; document that communication in the work order. 
- Create a follow up task labeled **“Emergency – Return Visit”** for **first thing next business day** and notify **Maria/Jaen** in the **Urgent Work Order group chat**. 

Política de Gestión de Emergencias y Solicitudes de Mantenimiento

**Propósito**

Proteger el bienestar de los residentes, preservar el valor de la propiedad y garantizar una rendición de cuentas clara tanto en situaciones de mantenimiento estándar como de emergencia.

**1) Canales y Recepción de Servicios (Cómo deben solicitar servicio los residentes)**

**Opciones para residentes**

- **App Folio**: Enviar una solicitud de servicio en línea. 
- **Línea de Mantenimiento (737) 5204891**: Centro de llamadas de tercero; **atención en inglés y español**. 

**Qué ocurre tras el envío**

- La solicitud se **registra en App Folio** (visible para seguimiento del residente). 
- Se **asigna automáticamente** al técnico correspondiente. 
- El técnico asignado recibe un **mensaje de texto/llamada** con los detalles de la solicitud. 

**Si los residentes escriben por correo o mensaje al personal**

- El personal debe **dirigir a los residentes** a App Folio o a la Línea de Mantenimiento. 
- **No** envíe una solicitud **en nombre del residente**. Las solicitudes internas **no** se asignan automáticamente al personal **de guardia** y generan riesgo de retraso. 
- **Órdenes de trabajo internas (solo para asuntos generales del inmueble):** 
- Las **ingresan únicamente Jaen o la Coordinadora de Mantenimiento (Maria)**, quienes son responsables del seguimiento y la acción. 
- Si considera que un asunto general requiere una orden interna, **envíe un mensaje a Maria y a Jaen** con los detalles; ellos la ingresarán y asignarán. 
- **Excepción (poco común):** Si **Jaen lo instruye expresamente** a registrar un asunto general, asígnelo a **Maria y Jaen** (solo según la indicación de Jaen). 

**2) Qué se considera una emergencia**

Los residentes deben seleccionar **“Urgent” (Urgente)** en App Folio para emergencias. El personal debe verificar que la situación **coincida con la lista siguiente o razonablemente represente un riesgo urgente de salud/seguridad**.

**Ejemplos (no exhaustivo):**

- **Inundación activa o tuberías reventadas**, o agua que **no puede contenerse**. 
- **Fugas u olor a gas**. 
- **Pérdida total de energía** en el **apartamento/habitación** o en **electrodomésticos esenciales** (p. ej., **refrigerador, estufa**). 
- **Incendio o riesgos de incendio** (incluidos humo u olores a quemado). 
- **Riesgos de seguridad** (p. ej., puertas/ventanas rotas; **no se puede asegurar** el apartamento). 
- **Respaldo de aguas negras** o **contaminación de agua** dentro o fuera de la unidad. 
- **Quedarse fuera sin llaves (lockout)**. 
- **Inodoro inoperante en unidad con un solo baño**. 
- **Filtraciones importantes en techo**. 
- Pérdida de **servicios básicos**: **electricidad, gas, agua, alcantarillado, drenaje**. 
- **Sin aire acondicionado con temperatura exterior > 85 °F** o **sin calefacción con temperatura < 65 °F**. 
- Cualquier condición que presente un **riesgo inmediato para la salud o la seguridad**. 

**Uso indebido de los canales de emergencia**

Los residentes que usen indebidamente el proceso de emergencia podrán recibir orientación sobre el uso correcto. El personal debe verificar si la solicitud cumple con el estándar anterior o **razonablemente** parece urgente.

**3) Acciones inmediatas cuando reciba un reporte de emergencia**

**En sitio (horario laboral o fuera de horario)**

1. **Ayude al residente a llamar de inmediato a la Línea de Mantenimiento.** Asegúrese de que pueda completar la llamada. 
1. Si por un problema del sistema debe registrarse la solicitud con urgencia, **avise a su líder de equipo**, luego contacte a **Maria y a Jaen** para instrucciones. 
1. **La persona que aprueba (Maria/Jaen)** **creará y asignará** la orden de trabajo para que usted la atienda de inmediato o la reasigne, según el caso. 
1. **Nunca** registre una emergencia como **orden interna**; las entradas internas **no** se enrutan al personal **de guardia**. 

**Fuera de horario, en persona**

- Ayude al residente a llamar a la línea de emergencia. **No** registre la solicitud manualmente. 
- Si el asunto es claramente urgente, **mande mensaje a su líder de equipo, a Maria y a Jaen** para aprobación/asignación. 

**Escalamiento de respaldo (indisponibilidad)**

- Si la **Coordinadora de Mantenimiento (Maria)** no está disponible por **más de 15 minutos** durante una emergencia, escale a **Jaen**, y luego a **Bekah (Rebekah)**. 

**4) Estándares de guardia y cobertura**

- En llamadas de emergencia, se espera que los técnicos estén **en sitio dentro de 1 hora** de haber recibido la llamada; **nunca más de 2 horas**. 
- Los técnicos **de guardia** deben estar **sobrios y totalmente disponibles** durante todo el periodo de guardia. 
- Los turnos **de guardia no pueden intercambiarse** salvo **aprobación del Gerente de Propiedad** y actualización en el **Calendario de Guardias**. 
- Si el técnico asignado está saturado, **escale de inmediato a su supervisor** y solicite apoyo; la falta de disponibilidad **no** es motivo aceptable de demora. Asegure la cobertura. 

**5) Acceso y requisitos de documentación (No deje sin resolver asuntos de vida/seguridad)**

**Documentación obligatoria en toda orden de emergencia**

- **Horas de llegada y salida**. 
- **Fotos del lugar** (cuando aplique). 
- **Descripción del problema encontrado**. 
- **Pasos realizados** para resolver o contener. 
- **Fotos** que respalden el trabajo realizado (cuando aplique). 
- **Notas de escalamiento** si alguna parte queda pendiente. _No dejamos asuntos de vida/seguridad sin escalar a los supervisores para confirmar próximos pasos._ 

**Acciones del equipo de arrendamiento (cuando deba escalarse una orden urgente ya ingresada)**

- Agregar una **nota** en la orden. 
- **Escalar en el chat grupal de Órdenes Urgentes**. 
- Si no hay respuesta oportuna, **escalar a Jaen** en el mismo chat. 

**Acceso y entrada durante una emergencia activa**

- Los técnicos deben **ingresar a la unidad** para atender una emergencia activa. 
- Si **las llaves del residente no funcionan** y el residente **no responde** tras múltiples intentos (**llamadas/mensajes**), **perfore la cerradura** para evitar mayores daños. 
- **En horario laboral:** contacte a **Maria** para coordinación y siguientes pasos. 
- **Fuera de horario:** escale a **Jaen**, luego a **Bekah**, para coordinar, **comunicar al residente** y gestionar **entrega/manejo de llaves**. 
- **Escale de inmediato** a su supervisor cuando se perfore una cerradura. Coordine **devolver o entregar una llave al residente**; no abandone la situación sin un plan de acceso seguro. 

**6) Escalamiento a proveedores (fuera del alcance del equipo)**

- Si el problema supera el alcance del equipo de mantenimiento: **escale a Jaen**. 
- Si **Jaen** no está disponible, escale a **Bekah**. 
- Se gestionará y enviará el **proveedor con licencia** correspondiente. Documente todas las acciones del proveedor en la orden de trabajo. 

**7) Protocolo ante picos de emergencias**

- Durante eventos de alto volumen (**incluyendo clima inclemente**), se puede solicitar apoyo al personal que **no** está de guardia. 
- Se espera apoyo de **todo** el equipo. **Son los hogares de las personas: actuemos con urgencia y empatía.** 

**8) Responsabilidad y disciplina**

- Dado que las emergencias impactan directamente la **vida y seguridad** de los residentes, las infracciones a esta política conllevan **consecuencias severas**: 
- **Acción disciplinaria escrita y/o suspensión** (como mínimo). 
- Hasta la **terminación inmediata**, según la gravedad. 
- No escalar o no responder adecuadamente puede resultar en **responsabilidad legal** y graves **riesgos de vida/seguridad**. En caso de duda, **es mejor sobreescalar y aprender** que subescalar y dejar a los residentes en condiciones peligrosas. 

**9) Materiales fuera de horario, compras y seguridad del residente**

**Autorización de compras fuera de horario**

- Cuando la resolución de la emergencia requiera **materiales/herramientas no disponibles fuera de horario**, obtenga aprobación para comprar. **Los pagos fuera de horario pueden ser realizados por Jaen o Bekah.** 
- Documente la aprobación en la orden (**nombre del aprobador, hora, monto/límite**) y adjunte foto del **recibo/comprobante** el siguiente día hábil. Siga el proceso de tarjeta corporativa o de reembolso aprobado, según se indique. 

**Si las tiendas están cerradas hasta la mañana**

- **No deje a los residentes en condiciones inseguras.** Antes de postergar la atención hasta la apertura, **agote todas las vías razonables** para mitigar el problema: 
- Verifique **inventario disponible**, existencias en comunidades vecinas, cajas de suministros de guardia y cualquier **proveedor 24 horas**. 
- Considere enviar un **proveedor con licencia** si la demora crea riesgo de vida/seguridad o daño sustancial a la propiedad; escale a **Jaen** (luego a **Bekah** si Jaen no está disponible). 
- Si la postergación es realmente inevitable, **deje la unidad en la condición más segura posible**, lo que puede incluir: 
- Cerrar el agua en el **accesorio** y/o **llave general de la unidad**; instalar **tapones/contención temporales**; colocar **señalización de advertencia**. 
- **Aislar riesgos eléctricos**; asegurar puertas/ventanas/cerraduras; proporcionar **mitigación temporal** (p. ej., equipo portátil de **aire acondicionado** o **calefacción**, herrajes temporales de cerradura) con la aprobación correspondiente. 
- Comunicar una **ETA** para la reparación permanente y la **hora de la visita de seguimiento**; documente dicha comunicación en la orden.

records.fullText:
# Emergency Work Order (WO) Process

## Purpose

To ensure all emergency maintenance requests are acknowledged, assigned, escalated, and resolved promptly while maintaining resident safety, protecting property, and ensuring accountability across the Maintenance team.

---

# Emergency Work Order Submission

Residents may submit emergency maintenance requests through:

- AppFolio (marked as “Urgent”)
- Maintenance Hotline

Once submitted:

- The Work Order is logged in AppFolio
- The emergency request is auto-assigned to the appropriate technician
- The assigned technician receives notification via text/call

Emergency Work Orders must never remain unaccepted or unattended.

---

# WEEKDAY EMERGENCY PROCESS (Business Hours)

## 1. Assigned Maintenance Technician Responsibility

During weekdays/business hours, the assigned Maintenance Technician is responsible for:

- Monitoring incoming emergency Work Orders
- Accepting the emergency WO immediately
- Contacting the resident if needed
- Responding onsite within company response standards
- Taking immediate action to resolve or contain the issue
- Updating and documenting all actions in the Work Order

Required documentation includes:

- Arrival and departure times
- Photos (when applicable)
- Resolution notes
- Escalation notes if unresolved

---

## 2. Escalation – Maintenance Coordinator (Eddie)

If the assigned technician does not accept or action the emergency WO promptly:

- Maintenance Coordinator (Eddie) will:
    - Accept the emergency WO
    - Coordinate directly with the assigned technician
    - Ensure the issue is actively being addressed
    - Monitor progress until stabilization or completion

If vendor coordination or additional support is needed, Eddie will escalate accordingly.

---

## 3. Supervisor Escalation

If Eddie is unavailable:

- The Supervisor will take over responsibility for:
    - Monitoring emergency WO activity
    - Accepting and assigning emergency WOs
    - Coordinating response efforts
    - Ensuring resident communication and mitigation steps are completed

If additional escalation is needed:

- Escalate to Bekah (Rebekah)

---

# WEEKEND / AFTER-HOURS ON-CALL PROCESS

## 1. On-Call Maintenance Technician Responsibility

During weekends, holidays, and after-hours periods, the assigned on-call Maintenance Technician is required to:

- Monitor all emergency calls and notifications continuously
- Accept and action emergency WOs immediately
- Remain sober and fully available during the entire on-call shift
- Contact residents when necessary
- Respond onsite within emergency response standards
- Mitigate or resolve emergency situations immediately
- Document all actions taken in the Work Order

On-call technicians are expected to:

- Arrive onsite within 1 hour whenever possible
- Never exceed 2 hours response time

---

## 2. Escalation – Maintenance Coordinator (Eddie)

If the on-call technician fails to accept or respond to the emergency WO:

- Eddie will:
    - Accept the emergency WO
    - Contact and coordinate with the on-call technician
    - Ensure emergency response is actively occurring
    - Assist with escalation or reassignment if needed

---

## 3. Supervisor & Leadership Escalation

If Eddie is unavailable during after-hours emergencies:

- The Supervisor will immediately assume responsibility for:
    - Monitoring emergency activity
    - Coordinating technician response
    - Managing escalations
    - Ensuring emergency mitigation and resident communication

If leadership escalation is required:

1. Escalate to Bekah (Rebekah)

---

# Emergency Examples

Examples of emergency situations include:

- Active flooding or burst pipes
- Gas leaks or gas odors
- Fire, smoke, or electrical hazards
- Sewer backups
- Major roof leaks
- Broken doors/windows affecting security
- Lockouts
- No HVAC during extreme temperatures
- Utility outages affecting safety
- Any immediate health or safety concern

---

# Accountability & Documentation

All emergency Work Orders require complete documentation, including:

- Arrival/departure times
- Photos
- Detailed repair or mitigation notes
- Communication and escalation notes
- Vendor involvement (if applicable)

Life safety issues must never be left unresolved without supervisor escalation and approval of next steps.

Failure to properly respond, escalate, or document emergency situations may result in disciplinary action due to the seriousness of resident safety and property risk.

---

# Emergency Workflow Summary

## Weekdays (Business Hours)

1. Emergency WO submitted
1. Assigned Maintenance Technician accepts and actions WO
1. If no response → Eddie intervenes
1. If Eddie unavailable → Supervisor takes over
1. Escalate to Bekah if needed
1. Emergency resolved and documented

---

## Weekends / After-Hours (On-Call)

1. Emergency WO submitted via AppFolio or Hotline
1. On-call Maintenance Technician accepts and actions WO
1. If no response → Eddie intervenes
1. If Eddie unavailable → Supervisor takes over
1. Escalate to Bekah if needed
1. Emergency resolved and documented

============================================================

## Proceso de Órdenes de Trabajo (WO) de Emergencia

============================================================

## Propósito

Garantizar que todas las solicitudes de mantenimiento de emergencia sean reconocidas, asignadas, escaladas y resueltas de manera oportuna, manteniendo la seguridad de los residentes, protegiendo la propiedad y asegurando responsabilidad dentro del equipo de Mantenimiento.

---

# Envío de Solicitudes de Emergencia

Los residentes pueden enviar solicitudes de mantenimiento de emergencia a través de:

- AppFolio (marcando la solicitud como “Urgente”)
- Línea de Emergencias de Mantenimiento

Una vez enviada:

- La Orden de Trabajo se registra en AppFolio
- La solicitud de emergencia se asigna automáticamente al técnico correspondiente
- El técnico asignado recibe una notificación vía llamada o mensaje de texto

Las Órdenes de Trabajo de emergencia nunca deben permanecer sin aceptar o sin atención.

---

# PROCESO DE EMERGENCIA – DÍAS LABORABLES (HORARIO DE OFICINA)

## 1. Responsabilidad del Técnico de Mantenimiento Asignado

Durante los días laborables y horario de oficina, el Técnico de Mantenimiento asignado es responsable de:

- Monitorear las Órdenes de Trabajo de emergencia entrantes
- Aceptar inmediatamente la WO de emergencia
- Contactar al residente si es necesario
- Llegar al sitio dentro de los estándares de respuesta de la compañía
- Tomar acción inmediata para resolver o contener el problema
- Actualizar y documentar todas las acciones realizadas en la Orden de Trabajo

La documentación requerida incluye:

- Hora de llegada y salida
- Fotografías (cuando aplique)
- Notas de resolución
- Notas de escalación si el problema no se resuelve

---

## 2. Escalación – Coordinador de Mantenimiento (Eddie)

Si el técnico asignado no acepta o atiende la WO de emergencia oportunamente:

- El Coordinador de Mantenimiento (Eddie):
    - Aceptará la WO de emergencia
    - Coordinará directamente con el técnico asignado
    - Confirmará que el problema esté siendo atendido activamente
    - Supervisará el progreso hasta la estabilización o resolución completa

Si se requiere apoyo adicional o coordinación con proveedores, Eddie realizará la escalación correspondiente.

---

## 3. Escalación al Supervisor

Si Eddie no está disponible:

- El Supervisor asumirá la responsabilidad de:
    - Monitorear la actividad de las WOs de emergencia
    - Aceptar y asignar las WOs de emergencia
    - Coordinar la respuesta del equipo
    - Garantizar comunicación con el residente y acciones de mitigación

Si se requiere una escalación adicional:

- Escalar a Bekah (Rebekah)

---

# PROCESO DE EMERGENCIA – FINES DE SEMANA / DESPUÉS DE HORARIO (ON-CALL)

## 1. Responsabilidad del Técnico On-Call

Durante fines de semana, días festivos y horarios fuera de oficina, el Técnico de Mantenimiento On-Call es responsable de:

- Monitorear continuamente llamadas y notificaciones de emergencia
- Aceptar y atender inmediatamente las WOs de emergencia
- Permanecer sobrio y completamente disponible durante todo el turno on-call
- Contactar a los residentes cuando sea necesario
- Responder en sitio dentro de los tiempos establecidos
- Mitigar o resolver la emergencia inmediatamente
- Documentar todas las acciones realizadas en la Orden de Trabajo

Se espera que los técnicos on-call:

- Lleguen al sitio dentro de 1 hora cuando sea posible
- Nunca excedan 2 horas de tiempo de respuesta

---

## 2. Escalación – Coordinador de Mantenimiento (Eddie)

Si el técnico on-call no acepta o responde a la WO de emergencia:

- Eddie:
    - Aceptará la WO de emergencia
    - Contactará y coordinará con el técnico on-call
    - Confirmará que la respuesta de emergencia esté ocurriendo activamente
    - Ayudará con reasignaciones o escalaciones si es necesario

---

## 3. Escalación al Supervisor y Liderazgo

Si Eddie no está disponible durante una emergencia fuera de horario:

- El Supervisor asumirá inmediatamente la responsabilidad de:
    - Monitorear la actividad de emergencias
    - Coordinar la respuesta del técnico
    - Manejar escalaciones
    - Garantizar mitigación de la emergencia y comunicación con residentes

Si se requiere escalación adicional:

1. Escalar a Bekah (Rebekah)

---

# Ejemplos de Emergencias

Ejemplos de situaciones de emergencia incluyen:

- Inundaciones activas o tuberías rotas
- Fugas u olor a gas
- Incendios, humo o riesgos eléctricos
- Respaldos de drenaje o alcantarillado
- Goteras severas en el techo
- Puertas o ventanas dañadas que afecten la seguridad
- Residentes bloqueados fuera de la unidad
- Falta de A/C o calefacción en temperaturas extremas
- Pérdida de servicios esenciales
- Cualquier situación que represente un riesgo inmediato para la salud o seguridad

---

# Responsabilidad y Documentación

Todas las WOs de emergencia requieren documentación completa, incluyendo:

- Hora de llegada y salida
- Fotografías
- Notas detalladas de reparación o mitigación
- Registros de comunicación y escalación
- Participación de proveedores externos (si aplica)

Los problemas relacionados con seguridad o riesgo de vida nunca deben dejarse sin resolver sin aprobación y escalación al Supervisor.

El incumplimiento en responder, escalar o documentar correctamente una emergencia puede resultar en acciones disciplinarias debido al impacto potencial en la seguridad del residente y la propiedad.

---

# Resumen del Flujo de Emergencia

## Días Laborables (Horario de Oficina)

1. Se envía la WO de emergencia
1. El Técnico de Mantenimiento asignado acepta y atiende la WO
1. Si no hay respuesta → Eddie interviene
1. Si Eddie no está disponible → El Supervisor toma control
1. Escalar a Bekah
1. La emergencia se resuelve y documenta

---

## Fines de Semana / Después de Horario (On-Call)

1. Se envía la WO de emergencia mediante AppFolio o Hotline
1. El Técnico On-Call acepta y atiende la WO
1. Si no hay respuesta → Eddie interviene
1. Si Eddie no está disponible → El Supervisor toma control
1. Escalar a Bekah
1. La emergencia se resuelve y documenta

records.fullText:
## Purpose

To ensure all company-owned equipment valued at **over $500** is properly documented, monitored, and managed throughout its warranty period to maximize warranty coverage and reduce replacement costs.

## Scope

This procedure applies to all **new Inventory Equipment** entered into AppFolio with a purchase price of **more than $500**.

## Procedure

### 1. Create the Equipment Record

- Enter the new equipment item into the AppFolio **Inventory Equipment** module.
- Purchase a warranty for all qualifying equipment (over $500), when available.

### 2. Document the Warranty

Record the following information in the **Notes** section of the Inventory Equipment record:

- Warranty provider
- Warranty start date
- Warranty expiration date
- Coverage details (if applicable)
- Warranty or registration number (if available)

### 3. Store the Receipt

- Attach the purchase receipt to the Inventory Equipment record whenever possible.
- If the receipt cannot be attached, include a link in the **Notes** section to the corresponding **AppFolio Payable Transaction (Expense)** where the receipt is stored. This ensures the receipt can be easily located for future warranty claims.

### 4. Schedule a Warranty Review

- Create a **future activity** to inspect the equipment shortly before the warranty expires.
- During the inspection, determine whether the equipment has any defects or excessive wear that may qualify for a warranty claim.

### 5. Verify Warranty Before Replacement

Before replacing or purchasing a replacement for an existing equipment item:

- Review the Inventory Equipment record to determine whether the item is still under warranty.
- If the warranty is active and the issue is covered, submit a warranty claim before purchasing a replacement.

## Standard

For every company-owned equipment item valued at **over $500**, the following is required:

- Warranty purchased (when available).
- Warranty information documented in the Inventory Equipment **Notes**.
- Purchase receipt attached, or a link to the corresponding AppFolio Payable Transaction.
- A future activity scheduled before the warranty expiration date.
- Warranty status reviewed before replacing the equipment to determine whether a warranty claim should be filed.

Following this process helps protect company assets, maximize warranty benefits, and minimize unnecessary replacement expenses.

records.title: Maintenance Team Communication & Accountability Standards
records.fullText:
Ongoing communication gaps within the Maintenance team resulted in repeated follow-ups, delayed responses, and unresolved requests. Critical maintenance items required escalation to executive leadership due to lack of timely acknowledgment and updates. This created inefficiencies, increased frustration, and diverted leadership focus away from higher-level responsibilities.

## Learning

Timely acknowledgment and clear communication are essential to operational efficiency and leadership trust. When maintenance requests are not responded to promptly - even if the task cannot be completed immediately - it creates unnecessary escalation and impacts client, owner, and internal stakeholder relationships. Clear response standards are not micromanagement but a strategic necessity to support leadership and company operations.

## Action

- Established clear response-time expectations for emails, calls, texts, and WhatsApp messages during office hours.
- Reinforced the requirement to acknowledge receipt of requests, even when completion will be delayed.
- Implemented end-of-day checks to ensure all direct communications from Metric leadership and team members are acknowledged.
- Clarified escalation protocols and after-hours expectations for true emergencies.
- Offered one-on-one or formal meetings for further clarification and alignment.

## Behavior (or Benefit)

### Maintenance team members demonstrate improved accountability, responsiveness, and professionalism in daily communications. Leadership receives timely updates, reducing unnecessary follow-ups and escalations. This alignment strengthens trust, improves workflow efficiency, and ensures maintenance operations effectively support company goals and stakeholder satisfaction.
