records.fullText:
Prepared by: Arturo Mendoza, Maintenance Coordinator Source: Training session with Metric Accounting (Claudia), 07/15/2026 For: SLAB — Maintenance > Quality Control Checks for Work Orders

## 1. Purpose

Before any completed ("Work Done") work order can be billed, it must pass a Quality Control review. QC confirms that the work is properly documented, the technician's notes and hours make sense for the job described, and everything required (photos, parts, categorization) is in place.

## 2. Process Overview

1. Identify all Work Orders currently in **Work Done** status, oldest to newest.
1. Open each order individually (or pull a batch of 5–10 at a time).
1. Capture the full order page as a PDF (Chrome extension "Go Full Page" — scrolls and captures the entire page in one image/PDF instead of multiple screenshots).
1. Review the order against the checklist below.
1. Leave the appropriate note in AppFolio and set the status (Ready to Bill or Waiting).
1. At the end of a batch, produce a short report: which orders went Ready to Bill, which went to Waiting (and why), and any messages that still need to go to technicians for clarification.

## 3. QC Checklist (review every order against all of these)

### 3.1 Translation

- Technician notes and photo captions must read clearly in English.
- If already in English, no changes needed.
- If in Spanish, translate for clear meaning (not a literal word-for-word translation) — preserve the technical meaning. Keep the original Spanish note as well (in parentheses or directly below the English version) so nothing is lost.

### 3.2 Reasonable Time Check

- Compare the hours logged to the work described. Reference ranges:
    - Vacant unit walk: 0.1–0.3 hr
    - Simple pest control treatment: ~0.2 hr
    - A/C repair: 1–2 hr
    - Larger jobs (tub resurfacing, major plumbing, etc.): proportionally longer — judge against the photos and description.
- If the time doesn't match the description (too little time for a big job, or too much time for a small one), **do not approve**. Either escalate to Arturo or request direct justification from the technician before moving to Ready to Bill.

### 3.3 After-Hours Check

- Expand "Maintenance Performer Details" if the order has it.
- Only genuine emergencies qualify as after-hours.
- If an order is marked after-hours but isn't a real emergency: leave a note and move to **Waiting** — do not correct the field yourself.

### 3.4 GPS Photos

- Mandatory on every order (before/after, when applicable).
- Confirm photos have GPS data and match the correct property/unit.
- If there are no photos, or no GPS data, the order **cannot be approved** — move to Waiting.
- Always note how many photos were reviewed.

### 3.5 Parts / Materials Inventory

- Any new parts/materials used must be logged under the order's Purchase Order or Parts and Supplies section.
- If materials were clearly used (per photos/notes) but not logged, move to **Waiting**.
- **Exception:** if the material was already part of the property before the repair (e.g., matching tile pulled from the same unit, not from Metric's stock) it is **not billable** — leave a clarifying note instead of logging it as inventory.
- If it's unclear whether a material came from the property or was purchased by Metric, **ask the technician** — don't assume either way.

### 3.6 Equipment Inventory

- If photos show rented/loaner equipment (power washer, blower motor, window/floor A/C unit, pool equipment, etc.), it must be logged on the order.
- **Exception:** the leaf blower ("sopladora") used for grounds work is always logged at $0 — this is correct and intentional, done purely for traceability of who used it and where, not for billing.

### 3.7 Work Order Issue (Category)

- Review the "Issue" field. If it's empty or wrong, correct it using the list of valid values (see Section 5 below).
- If the field is empty, it's safe to fill in with confidence — there's no risk of losing data by completing it.

## 4. Decision Rules

### 4.1 Leave in Waiting (do not approve) when:

- Photos are missing.
- Parts/materials are missing from the log.
- Logged time isn't reasonable for the described work.
- The work order description and the technician's labor notes don't match/are inconsistent.
- The work looks incomplete (e.g., notes say "continuing tomorrow" with no follow-up labor entry).
- There's genuine doubt about whether the work was actually completed.

### 4.2 Mark Ready to Bill when:

- Translation is complete (English readable).
- GPS photos are confirmed.
- Logged time is reasonable.
- Parts and equipment are logged (except property-owned materials, which are noted but not billed).
- The Work Order Issue field is correct.

## 5. AppFolio Notes Format

- Every reviewed order gets a note documenting the QC review (what was checked, photo count, any relevant context).
- When moving to **Waiting**, always leave a note explaining exactly why (e.g., "missing parts log," "time not justified by description," etc.) — bilingual when it will be read by a technician.
- Notes should always be written ready to copy-paste directly into AppFolio.

## 6. Escalation Rules — When NOT to Decide Alone (escalate to Arturo)

- **Orders with notes from the previous coordinator (Eddie Castillo, terminated 06/22/2026)** and no independent verification: mark as suspicious and double-check. There's a documented pattern of inaccurate or incomplete notes from this person — give these extra scrutiny.
- **Resident cancelled the order, or paid for their own handyman:** do not change the status to "No Need to Bill" without permission — this also requires an AppFolio permission level not everyone has. Verify permissions before acting, and escalate if blocked.
- **Inconsistency between the order description and the technician's labor notes** (e.g., the description describes one problem, but the labor entry describes solving a different one): don't resolve this alone — escalate.
- **Any billing question beyond the property-material rule already explained above:** ask before deciding — don't guess.

## 7. Common Billing Precedents (already confirmed, for reference)

- **Property-owned materials** reused during a repair (e.g., matching tile that came from the same unit) — not billed, note only.
- **Portable A/C units** (window or floor) placed temporarily for a resident while a permanent repair is scheduled — these are Metric equipment and are **always billed** as a rental fee (confirmed ~$100/unit per use), UNLESS the portable unit itself already belonged to the property (in which case it's not billed). Confirm with Josué/Lyndsay if unsure which applies.
- **Drain snake/auger use** ("la guaya," "el cochinito"): technicians sometimes use this without logging it as a part/tool or assigning it a price. Flag to Josué to confirm whether it should be billed on that order.
- **Leaf blower ("sopladora")** used for grounds: always $0, correct, traceability only (see 3.6).

## 8. Batch Workflow Recap

1. Pull the oldest Work Done orders first.
1. Work in batches of 5–10: capture each as a PDF, review each against the checklist above, and record the decision (Ready to Bill / Waiting + reason).
1. At the end of the batch, compile: orders marked Ready to Bill, orders left in Waiting (with reasons), and any pending messages that need to go out to technicians for clarification.

records.title: Mandatory Reporting of Property Issues
records.author: Lyndsay Hanes
records.fullText:
Effective immediately, all maintenance personnel are required to document and report any issue identified at their assigned properties — **without exception**. The purpose of this policy is to ensure that all property concerns are promptly communicated to management so that corrective actions can be taken efficiently, property standards can be maintained, and ownership confidence can be preserved.

Each maintenance technician is responsible for inspecting their assigned properties daily, ensuring that all areas, systems, and assets are in good condition. Any issue observed — whether it is broken, unsafe, misplaced, or showing signs of deterioration — must be photographed and reported immediately in the designated Maintenance WhatsApp group. Reports must include a clear photo and a short description of the problem.

It is understood that some issues cannot be resolved immediately due to lack of time, tools, materials, or manpower. This is acceptable and will not be considered a performance failure. However, **failing to report an issue** is unacceptable and will be treated as a **failure to perform assigned duties**. Management and ownership must never discover unreported issues during site visits or inspections.

Additionally, **any sign of criminal activity must be reported immediately**, with special attention to **squatters, break-ins, or unsecured apartments** — whether the unit is vacant or occupied. These situations are **time-sensitive** and can lead to **serious property damage or safety risks in a very short period of time**. For that reason, both **law enforcement and management** must be notified right away to prevent further harm and to document the incident properly.

Examples of issues that must always be reported include, but are not limited to:

- Green or unmaintained swimming pools
- Fallen fences or damaged structures
- Bulk trash or debris visible on the property
- Any deferred maintenance or visible damage to the grounds or buildings
- Any suspected criminal activity, trespassing, or evidence of unauthorized access

If management is not informed about a problem, resources cannot be properly planned or allocated for its correction. For this reason, failure to report issues reflects directly on the technician’s performance and accountability. Continued noncompliance with this policy may result in disciplinary action.

All maintenance staff are reminded that part of their responsibility is not only to maintain the property but also to communicate its condition clearly and promptly. Reporting both positive and negative findings demonstrates professionalism, reliability, and respect for the properties under our care.

This is the final reminder regarding this matter. Every visit, every property, every time — all issues must be documented and reported without exception.

**Approved by:** Lyndsay Hanes

**Effective Date:** Immediately

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Política: Reporte obligatorio de problemas en las propiedades

Con efecto inmediato, todo el personal de mantenimiento está obligado a documentar y reportar cualquier problema identificado en sus propiedades asignadas — **sin excepciones**. El propósito de esta política es garantizar que todos los incidentes o deficiencias en las propiedades sean comunicados de manera oportuna a la administración, permitiendo tomar acciones correctivas con eficiencia, mantener los estándares de calidad y conservar la confianza de los propietarios.

Cada técnico de mantenimiento es responsable de inspeccionar sus propiedades diariamente, asegurándose de que todas las áreas, sistemas y activos estén en buenas condiciones. Cualquier situación observada — ya sea algo roto, inseguro, fuera de lugar o en mal estado — debe ser **fotografiada y reportada de inmediato** en el grupo designado de **WhatsApp de Mantenimiento**. El reporte debe incluir una fotografía clara y una breve descripción del problema.

Se entiende que algunos problemas no pueden resolverse de inmediato por falta de tiempo, herramientas, materiales o personal. Esto es completamente aceptable y **no se considerará una falla en el desempeño**. Sin embargo, **no reportar un problema detectado** es inaceptable y será tratado como un **incumplimiento de las responsabilidades asignadas**. Bajo ninguna circunstancia la gerencia o los propietarios deben descubrir problemas no reportados durante sus visitas o inspecciones.

Adicionalmente, **toda actividad delictiva o sospechosa debe reportarse de inmediato**, prestando especial atención a **personas ocupando ilegalmente una unidad (squatters), intentos de allanamiento o departamentos sin seguridad adecuada**, ya sea que se trate de una unidad **desocupada o habitada**. Estas situaciones son **de carácter urgente** y pueden causar **daños graves o riesgos de seguridad en muy poco tiempo**, por lo que es esencial que **las autoridades y la administración sean notificadas de inmediato** para evitar consecuencias mayores y documentar adecuadamente el incidente.

Ejemplos de problemas que deben reportarse de manera obligatoria incluyen, entre otros:

- Albercas verdes o en mal estado
- Cercas caídas o estructuras dañadas
- Basura o desechos voluminosos visibles en la propiedad
- Cualquier mantenimiento pendiente o deterioro evidente
- Cualquier actividad delictiva, allanamiento o acceso no autorizado

Si la administración no tiene conocimiento de un problema, no puede planificar ni asignar los recursos necesarios para resolverlo. Por ello, **la falta de reporte afecta directamente la evaluación del desempeño del técnico** y su nivel de responsabilidad. El incumplimiento continuo de esta política puede resultar en medidas disciplinarias.

El personal de mantenimiento debe recordar que su labor no solo consiste en mantener las propiedades, sino también en **comunicar claramente su estado**. Reportar tanto los aspectos positivos como los negativos refleja profesionalismo, compromiso y respeto hacia las propiedades bajo nuestra administración.

Esta es la última advertencia respecto a este tema. En cada visita, en cada propiedad, en todo momento — **todos los problemas deben ser documentados y reportados sin excepción**.

**Aprobado por:** Lyndsay Hanes

**Fecha de entrada en vigor:** Inmediata

Pull the report to find all work orders in "cancelled" status that has labor accumulated. There really is no reason a work order with labor should be cancelled if there is labor accumulated. Research each one - likely re-open them and bill the work order. If the labor was done and we should NOT be billing it, then it can be moved to "work done no bill needed" status.

Ideally this report will be at zero

**✅ Step-by-Step Procedure: Audit Cancelled Work Orders with Labor (Not Billed)**

**1. Access the Report**

- Open the [**AppFolio report**](https://metricpropertymanagement.appfolio.com/buffered_reports/228) for cancelled work orders with labor logged.
- This task is **recurring** (frequency not explicitly stated but implied to be regular).

**2. Review Each Work Order**

- Check for **time logs** (e.g., 0.5 hours).
- Determine the reason for cancellation:
    - **Duplicate work orders**.
    - **No longer needed** (e.g., task already handled by another team).
    - **Test accounts**.

**3. Verify Work Order Details**

- Open the work order and review:
    - **Technician notes**.
    - **Photos or attachments**.
    - **Context of cancellation** (e.g., trailer full, unable to complete task).

**4. Decide on Billing Action**

- If the task was **not completed** or **not needed**:
    - Click **“Mark Completed – No Bill Needed”**.
    - Add a note explaining the reason (e.g., test account, duplicate, unable to complete).
- If the task was **valid and completed**:
    - Confirm with **Jane or the Property Manager**.
    - If approved for billing:
        - Change status from **Cancelled** to **Waiting**.
        - Then click **“Mark Work Done”**.
        - Proceed to **“Mark Ready to Bill”**.

**5. Attach Supporting Evidence**

- Ensure **photos and time logs** are attached.
- If the technician is unavailable or photos were sent via WhatsApp:
    - You may attach them manually, but this is **not recommended**—technicians are expected to do this.

**6. Finalize Billing**

- Once marked as **Work Done** and **Ready to Bill**, the accounting team can process the billing.
- Ensure the correct rate is applied based on the technician’s logged hours.

records.title: Resident Lockout Procedure for Delinquent Accounts
records.fullText:
## Purpose

The purpose of a lockout is not to evict a resident. It is to gain the resident’s attention and require communication with the Collections Department regarding a seriously delinquent balance. Every lockout must be completed in full compliance with applicable law and company policy.

---

# Eligibility for Lockout

The Collections Department has sole authority to determine when a resident should be locked out.

A lockout may be authorized when:

- The resident has an outstanding balance exceeding $800.
- The resident has been unresponsive to collection efforts.
- It is on or after the 8th day of the month.

Only the Collections Department may initiate this process.

---

# Lockout Workflow / Work Order Process

### Step 1 – Collections Request

The Collections Department creates an **Activity** requesting a resident lockout.

### Step 2 – Work Order Assignment

The Maintenance Coordinator assigns the work order to the technician scheduled to be onsite at the property.

### Step 3 – Technician Performs Lockout

The assigned technician completes the lockout following the procedures below.

---

# Preferred Lockout Method

Whenever possible, use the **approved silver lock cover** (Home Depot Supply).

Use the lock cover whenever the apartment has a **round doorknob**.

### Benefits

- Fast installation
- Easily reversible
- No lock replacement required
- Minimal disruption to the resident

---

# Technician Procedure

Complete the following steps in order.

## 1. Post the Lockout Notice

Before leaving the apartment, post the approved **Resident Lockout Notice** on the exterior of the apartment door.

The notice must inform the resident:

- They have been locked out
- How to regain access
- That they must contact the office/Collections Department

---

## 2. Attempt Resident Contact

Knock on the apartment door.

If the resident answers:

- Inform them they must contact the office or Collections Department immediately.
- Remain courteous and professional.
- Do **not** discuss account balances or payment arrangements.

---

## 3. Perform the Lockout

Use the procedure appropriate for the apartment's lock hardware.

---

# Lock Type Procedures

## Round Doorknob

Install the approved silver lock cover over the existing doorknob.

**Do not change the lock.**

---

## Lever Handle with Kwikset SmartKey

If the apartment has:

- Lever handle
- Kwikset SmartKey lock

The technician should:

1. Bring the designated vacant lock key before beginning. 
1. Rekey the existing lock to the vacant key.
1. Retain the resident's original key.
1. Keep the original key attached to the apartment key tag.
1. Do not discard the original key.

The original key will be needed to restore the lock once the resident contacts the office.

---

## Lever Handle Without Kwikset SmartKey

If the existing lock is **not** a Kwikset SmartKey lock:

1. Unlock the door if possible.
1. Remove or drill the existing lock when necessary.
1. Install a new Kwikset SmartKey lock.
1. Retain the resident's original key.
1. Label and store the original key with the apartment key tag.

The original key will be used when restoring the lock.

All replacement locks installed must be Kwikset SmartKey locks whenever possible.

---

# Documentation Requirements

Before closing the work order, technicians must:

- Add detailed work order notes.
- Upload clear photographs showing:
    - Posted lockout notice
    - Installed lock cover or replacement lock
    - Any unusual conditions encountered
- Clock out of the work order.

**Documentation is mandatory for every lockout.**

---

# Resident Re-Entry Requests

Texas law requires that residents be allowed back into their apartment after requesting re-entry following a lawful lockout.

**Company Standard**

Access must be restored **within two (2) hours** of the resident contacting the office.

This requirement applies:

- Business hours
- After hours
- Overnight
- Weekends
- Holidays

**There are no exceptions.**

Failure to restore access within two hours may cause the lockout to become an unlawful eviction.

---

# Emergency Re-Entry Procedure

When a resident requests access:

1. Office staff immediately dispatch Maintenance.
1. The responding technician treats the request as an emergency.
1. The technician restores access within **two hours** of the resident's request.

Prompt response is mandatory.

---

# Technician Communication During Re-Entry

When restoring access:

- Return the lock to its original configuration or key.
- Remain courteous and professional.
- Do not discuss payment arrangements.

Technicians should advise the resident:

"You will need to contact the Collections Department regarding your balance due."

If appropriate, technicians may also state:

"The purpose of the lockout is to get you in contact with the Collections Department. If your balance isn't addressed, I may be returning to perform another lockout."

Technicians must never:

- Negotiate payment arrangements
- Accept payments
- Debate account balances
- Make promises regarding the resident's account

All financial discussions must be handled by the **Collections Department**.

---

# Compliance Reminder - Important Legal Reminder

A resident lockout **is not an eviction**.

It is a legally regulated collections process intended to encourage communication with the Collections Department.

Because of the legal requirements surrounding lockouts:

- Follow this SOP exactly.
- Document every action.
- Respond immediately to re-entry requests.
- Restore access within two hours every time.

**Failure to meet the two-hour restoration requirement may expose the company to claims of an unlawful eviction and legal liability.**

## Resident Answers the Door Before Lockout Can Be Completed

If the resident answers the door before the lockout can be completed:

- Remain courteous and professional.
- Advise the resident to contact the office or Collections Department immediately.
- Inform the resident:
- "Please contact the office or the Collections Department regarding your account. If the matter is not resolved, I will be returning to complete the lockout."
- Do not discuss balances or payment arrangements.
- Report the unsuccessful attempt to the assigned Collections Agent.
- Attempt the lockout again during the technician's next scheduled onsite visit.
- Do not make a special trip solely to perform the lockout unless specifically directed by Management or the Collections Department.
- Continue attempting the lockout until the Collections Department instructs Maintenance to stop or the lockout is successfully completed.

## Lockout Completed Prior to Eviction Status Change

If a resident is moved to the formal eviction process **after** the lockout has already been completed:

- Do not reverse or remove the completed lockout.
- If the lock was rekeyed or replaced, leave it in its current condition.
- If the original lock was drilled because no key was available, it does not need to be restored.
- If the resident requests access or keys, direct them to the office to obtain the appropriate key or further instructions.
- Any decision to discontinue future lockout activities must come from the Collections Department.

---

## Key Takeaways

- Lockouts may only be authorized by the **Collections Department**.
- Lockouts are intended to encourage communication—not to evict residents.
- Use the **silver lock cover** whenever a round doorknob is present.
- Preserve the resident's original key whenever a lock is rekeyed or replaced.
- Complete all required documentation before closing the work order.
- Re-entry requests are emergencies and must be completed within **two hours**, regardless of the time or day.
- Maintenance staff must never discuss balances or negotiate payments with residents.

# SOP: Procedimiento de Bloqueo de Acceso para Residentes con Cuentas Morosas

## Propósito

El propósito de un bloqueo de acceso **no es desalojar a un residente**. Su finalidad es llamar la atención del residente y exigir que se comunique con el Departamento de Cobros con respecto a un saldo seriamente vencido. Todo bloqueo de acceso debe realizarse en pleno cumplimiento de la legislación aplicable y de las políticas de la empresa.

---

# Elegibilidad para el Bloqueo de Acceso

El **Departamento de Cobros** tiene la autoridad exclusiva para determinar cuándo un residente debe ser bloqueado.

Un bloqueo de acceso puede autorizarse cuando:

- El residente tiene un saldo pendiente superior a **$800**.
- El residente no ha respondido a los intentos de cobro.
- Es el **día 8 del mes o una fecha posterior**.

**Solo el Departamento de Cobros puede iniciar este proceso.**

---

# Flujo del Proceso de Bloqueo / Orden de Trabajo

## Paso 1 – Solicitud del Departamento de Cobros

El Departamento de Cobros crea una **Actividad (Activity)** solicitando el bloqueo de acceso del residente.

## Paso 2 – Asignación de la Orden de Trabajo

El Coordinador de Mantenimiento asigna la orden de trabajo al técnico programado para estar en la propiedad.

## Paso 3 – El Técnico Realiza el Bloqueo

El técnico asignado completa el bloqueo siguiendo los procedimientos descritos a continuación.

---

# Método Preferido de Bloqueo

Siempre que sea posible, utilice la **cubierta plateada aprobada para cerraduras** (Home Depot Supply).

Utilice la cubierta cuando el apartamento tenga una **perilla redonda**.

### Beneficios

- Instalación rápida.
- Fácil de retirar.
- No requiere reemplazar la cerradura.
- Mínima interrupción para el residente.

---

# Procedimiento para el Técnico

Complete los siguientes pasos en orden.

## 1. Colocar el Aviso de Bloqueo

Antes de retirarse del apartamento, coloque el **Aviso de Bloqueo para Residentes** aprobado en la parte exterior de la puerta.

El aviso debe informar al residente:

- Que su acceso ha sido bloqueado.
- Cómo recuperar el acceso.
- Que debe comunicarse con la oficina o con el Departamento de Cobros.

---

## 2. Intentar Contactar al Residente

Toque la puerta del apartamento.

Si el residente responde:

- Indíquele que debe comunicarse inmediatamente con la oficina o con el Departamento de Cobros.
- Mantenga una actitud cortés y profesional.
- **No** discuta saldos pendientes ni acuerdos de pago.

---

## 3. Realizar el Bloqueo

Utilice el procedimiento correspondiente según el tipo de cerradura del apartamento.

---

# Procedimientos Según el Tipo de Cerradura

## Perilla Redonda

- Instale la cubierta plateada aprobada sobre la perilla existente.
- **No cambie la cerradura.**

---

## Manija Tipo Palanca con Kwikset SmartKey

Si el apartamento tiene:

- Manija tipo palanca.
- Cerradura **Kwikset SmartKey**.

El técnico debe:

- Llevar la llave designada para unidades vacantes antes de comenzar.
- Reconfigurar (rekey) la cerradura existente para que funcione con la llave de unidades vacantes.
- Conservar la llave original del residente.
- Mantener la llave original junto con la etiqueta de llaves del apartamento.
- No desechar la llave original.

La llave original será necesaria para restaurar la cerradura cuando el residente se comunique con la oficina.

---

## Manija Tipo Palanca sin Kwikset SmartKey

Si la cerradura existente **no** es una Kwikset SmartKey:

- Desbloquee la puerta si es posible.
- Retire o perfore la cerradura existente cuando sea necesario.
- Instale una nueva cerradura Kwikset SmartKey.
- Conserve la llave original del residente.
- Etiquete y almacene la llave original junto con la etiqueta de llaves del apartamento.

La llave original se utilizará para restaurar la cerradura posteriormente.

Siempre que sea posible, todas las cerraduras de reemplazo deben ser **Kwikset SmartKey**.

---

# Requisitos de Documentación

Antes de cerrar la orden de trabajo, los técnicos deben:

- Agregar notas detalladas en la orden de trabajo.
- Subir fotografías claras que muestren:
    - El aviso de bloqueo colocado.
    - La cubierta de cerradura instalada o la nueva cerradura.
    - Cualquier condición inusual encontrada.
- Registrar la salida (Clock Out) de la orden de trabajo.

**La documentación es obligatoria para cada bloqueo de acceso.**

---

# Solicitudes de Reingreso del Residente

La legislación de Texas exige que los residentes puedan volver a ingresar a su apartamento después de solicitar el restablecimiento del acceso tras un bloqueo realizado legalmente.

## Estándar de la Empresa

El acceso debe restablecerse **dentro de las dos (2) horas** posteriores a que el residente se comunique con la oficina.

Este requisito aplica durante:

- Horario laboral.
- Después del horario laboral.
- Durante la noche.
- Fines de semana.
- Días festivos.

**No existen excepciones.**

No restablecer el acceso dentro de las dos horas puede convertir el bloqueo en un desalojo ilegal.

---

# Procedimiento de Reingreso de Emergencia

Cuando un residente solicite acceso:

- El personal de oficina debe despachar inmediatamente al equipo de Mantenimiento.
- El técnico debe tratar la solicitud como una emergencia.
- El técnico debe restaurar el acceso dentro de las dos horas posteriores a la solicitud del residente.

**Una respuesta rápida es obligatoria.**

---

# Comunicación del Técnico Durante el Reingreso

Al restaurar el acceso:

- Devuelva la cerradura a su configuración o llave original.
- Mantenga una actitud cortés y profesional.
- No discuta acuerdos de pago.

El técnico debe informar al residente:

"Necesitará comunicarse con el Departamento de Cobros con respecto al saldo pendiente de su cuenta."

Si corresponde, también puede decir:

"El propósito del bloqueo es ponerlo en contacto con el Departamento de Cobros. Si su saldo pendiente no se atiende, es posible que tenga que regresar para realizar otro bloqueo."

Los técnicos **nunca deben**:

- Negociar acuerdos de pago.
- Aceptar pagos.
- Debatir saldos de la cuenta.
- Hacer promesas sobre la cuenta del residente.

Todas las conversaciones financieras deben ser manejadas exclusivamente por el Departamento de Cobros.

---

# Recordatorio de Cumplimiento – Aviso Legal Importante

Un bloqueo de acceso **no es un desalojo**.

Es un proceso de cobro regulado por la ley cuyo propósito es fomentar la comunicación con el Departamento de Cobros.

Debido a los requisitos legales relacionados con los bloqueos:

- Siga este SOP exactamente como está escrito.
- Documente cada acción realizada.
- Responda inmediatamente a las solicitudes de reingreso.
- Restaure el acceso dentro de las dos horas en todos los casos.

El incumplimiento del requisito de restaurar el acceso dentro de las dos horas puede exponer a la empresa a reclamaciones por desalojo ilegal y responsabilidad legal.

## El Residente Abre la Puerta Antes de Completar el Bloqueo

Si el residente abre la puerta antes de que el técnico pueda completar el bloqueo:

- Mantenga una actitud cortés y profesional.
- Indique al residente que debe comunicarse inmediatamente con la oficina o con el Departamento de Cobros.
- Puede decirle al residente:

"Por favor comuníquese con la oficina o con el Departamento de Cobros respecto a su cuenta. Si el asunto no se resuelve, regresaré para completar el bloqueo."

- No discuta saldos pendientes ni acuerdos de pago.
- Informe al agente de Cobros asignado que el intento no pudo completarse.
- Intente nuevamente el bloqueo durante la próxima visita programada del técnico a la propiedad.
- No realice un viaje especial únicamente para efectuar el bloqueo, a menos que la Gerencia o el Departamento de Cobros lo indiquen expresamente.
- Continúe intentando realizar el bloqueo hasta que el Departamento de Cobros indique detener el proceso o el bloqueo se complete exitosamente.

## Bloqueo Completado Antes de un Cambio al Proceso de Desalojo

Si un residente es enviado al proceso formal de desalojo **después** de que el bloqueo ya fue realizado:

- No revierta ni retire el bloqueo ya completado.
- Si la cerradura fue reconfigurada (rekey) o reemplazada, déjela en su estado actual.
- Si fue necesario perforar la cerradura porque no se contaba con la llave original, no es necesario restaurarla.
- Si el residente solicita acceso o sus llaves, indíquele que debe pasar por la oficina para recoger las llaves o recibir instrucciones adicionales.
- Cualquier decisión de cancelar futuros intentos de bloqueo deberá provenir exclusivamente del Departamento de Cobros.

---

# Puntos Clave

- Solo el Departamento de Cobros puede autorizar un bloqueo de acceso.
- Los bloqueos buscan fomentar la comunicación, **no desalojar** a los residentes.
- Utilice la cubierta plateada siempre que exista una perilla redonda.
- Conserve siempre la llave original del residente cuando una cerradura sea reconfigurada o reemplazada.
- Complete toda la documentación requerida antes de cerrar la orden de trabajo.
- Las solicitudes de reingreso son emergencias y deben completarse dentro de las dos horas, sin importar la hora o el día.
- El personal de Mantenimiento nunca debe discutir saldos pendientes ni negociar pagos con los residentes.

records.title: Move-Out, Vacancy Confirmation, and Deposit Refund
records.fullText:
### 1. Purpose

To establish clear procedures for confirming vacancies, conducting move-out inspections, and ensuring timely deposit refunds in compliance with company policies and applicable state regulations.

---

### 2. Scope

This SOP applies to all **Collections Managers**, **Maintenance Technicians**, and **Make Ready Technicians**.

---

### 3. Policy Overview

- Maintenance and Make Ready Technicians are **not responsible** for confirming or determining unit vacancy.
- All vacancies must be **confirmed by a Collections Manager** before any maintenance staff are dispatched for lock changes or make-ready work.

---

### 4. Procedures

A. Vacancy Confirmation

- A **Collections Manager** must confirm that the unit is officially vacant **before scheduling any lock change or work order**.
- Confirmation should include:
    1. Verification of move-out in the property management system.
    1. Physical inspection confirming the unit is empty.
- If a technician’s assistance is needed during the inspection (e.g., for lockout support), this must be **pre-arranged** with both parties’ schedules.

---

B. Move-Out Inspection

- The **Collections Manager** is solely responsible for completing the move-out inspection.
- Maintenance and Make Ready Technicians **must not perform or document** move-out inspections.
- Inspections must be completed in the **Folio system**, including:
    - Detailed notes
    - Photos
    - Videos (if applicable)

---

C. Move-Out Documentation and Reconciliation

- Upon completion of the inspection:
    1. The Collections Manager must prepare and submit the **Move-Out Inspection Report**.
    1. A **Final Account Reconciliation** must be completed and sent to the resident within **5–10 business days** of the move-out date.
    1. The entire process must **not exceed 15 business days**.

---

D. Deposit Refund

- Residents must receive their **deposit refund within 30 days** of the move-out date.
- All documentation (inspection report, reconciliation, and refund confirmation) must be **uploaded to the resident’s file**.

records.title: 21-Day Turn Process (Upgrade Units)
records.fullText:
If you **_plan ahead_** then you should be able to have purchase orders entered AND approved _well before the apartment is vacated_. For instance, you get a notice to vacate, you pre-walk the apartment 30 days before the vacate date, per the 21-Day Turn task in Asana.

- [ ] **Pre-Walk Units 30 Days Before Vacating**: You document the scope to turn the apartment via the Asana form on the Property Board in Asana. 
- [ ] **Order All Materials**: You make a cart with Amazon or Ferguson, you enter a PO in ResMan. If the order exceeds $300, you want for supervisor approval, which should be happening 2-3 times a week. If it does not happen, make your supervisor a task in Asana for this item. Mark it “Ask for help.” Get the PO number once approved, enter it in your order, order. _You will never have parts delays if you follow this process_. Of course, you may have an unexpected move out, but that is the exception to the rule. 
- [ ] **Schedule All Turn Services with Vendors**: Schedule paint, clean, flooring, resurfacing and heavy repairs with your turn vendors. Enter a PO and formalize the scheduling once you have a PO approval. 
- [ ] **Update the ResMan Make Ready Board**: Enter the scope, vendor, date scheduled (IF scheduled, and PO number. See the instructions for managing and updating the Make Ready Board here. 
- [ ] **Schedule Electric to be Connected the 1st day of vacancy.**

If you have a heavy turn and you are contracting the work out, sheetrock repairs, full/heavy paint, and it exceeds $300- you would almost always know this a month in advance. We trust you have worked out relationships with turn vendors and have agreed pricing. _Not every item is a bid item_. If your price sheet doesn’t cover the scope of work needed, get a verbal or written bid and approve only that amount to the vendor, once your supervisor approves it. Again, you have 30 days to prepare for this so delays are not acceptable.

This applies to upgrades. Upgrades we will agree on a turn scope and timeline, ranging from 14-21 days and no more than 21 days.

records.title: Approved Company Platforms and Applications
records.fullText:
As a company Metric has strategically evaluated and selected specific platforms and applications for ease of use, collaboration, cost and systems administration. As such, the following Applications and Platforms Policy is in place.

**Purpose:**

To ensure data security, operational consistency, and compliance with company standards, all employees must use only company-approved applications and platforms for work-related activities.

If any employee has a recommendation for an application or platform, they are welcome to contact management for consideration.

---

**1. Approved Platforms for Core Functions**

Employees are required to use the following platforms for designated tasks:

- **Email:** Employees are strictly to use their company assigned email address for all company related communication from internal communication, to residents, vendors or clients. Use of a personal email address for any company related matter is strictly forbidden. 
- **Document Signing:** Only **Adobe Sign** is approved for initiating electronic signatures. Use of any other online signing platform when initiating online signatures is strictly prohibited.
- **Online Meetings:** Only **Microsoft Teams** is approved for initiating online meetings. 
- **Meeting Notetakers:** Only **Microsoft Teams/M365 Copilot** is approved. Use of external notetaking apps (e.g., Otter.AI, Evernote, Notion) is not permitted.
- **Phone Communication:** All calls to residents must be made using the company-issued **RingCentral** line. Under no circumstance is an employee to use their personal cell phone to make or receive calls or texts to/from residents or vendors. 
- **Text Messaging:** All resident text communications must be conducted through **AppFolio**.
- **Payment Processing:** Employees must not accept payments via **Apple Pay**, **Venmo**, **Cash App**, or any other unapproved platform under any circumstances. All payments must be made through Appfolio. 
- **Messaging Channels:** All **WhatsApp** communications must occur within approved **Metric community channels** only.
- **Password Managers:** The only approved password manager is LastPass. Google Password Manager is not approved and should never be used to save passwords. 
- **Reports:** Only Microsoft platforms such as Excel, and Word will be used for report purposes.

---

**2. Unauthorized Software and Services**

- Installation or use of personal or unapproved software on company devices is prohibited.
- Any unauthorized hardware or software may be removed without notice.
- Exceptions must be approved by senior management.

records.fullText:
Cold water temperature from a sink or faucet typically depends on the season and local water supply, but here are general guidelines:

•	💧 Typical range: 50°F to 70°F (10°C to 21°C)

•	❄ In colder climates or during winter: It can drop as low as 40°F (4°C) or even 35°F (1.6°C) if the pipes are close to the exterior walls or underground supply.

•	🌞 In warmer climates or summer: It can rise to 70°F–80°F (21°C–27°C).

If you’re testing for building maintenance or safety, most standards say:

•	Below 80°F (27°C) is considered acceptable for cold water.

•	Above 80°F (27°C) might indicate heat transfer from hot water lines, poor insulation, or recirculation issues.

Always search inventory thoroughly before adding new inventory to make sure we do not have an item in place we can use.

Inventory vs. One Time Items

If a single item is purchased for a work order or a specialty item is purchased that is not regularly used and will not be stocked, do not add it to inventory, send the receipt to accounting and make sure to add the work order number and markup to the expense. This will keep our inventory list shorter.

Adding Inventory

Naming Conformity

The name should start with the actual item (the way a tech would search for it), not the brand. For items that are size specific like blinds and doors the item starts with the size. For instance:

DO NOT NAME THIS WAY: _Seasons Anchor Point 24" Brushed Nickel Towel Bar, Tollet Paper Holder, Towel Ring 3 Piece Kit*_

NAME THIS WAY: _Bathroom Kit 3 Piece Brushed Nickel_

Then add description: _Seasons Anchor Brand 24" towel bar, toilet paper holder, towel ring_

DO NOT NAME THIS WAY: 1-3/4" OD Faucet Hole Cover

NAME THIS WAY: Faucet Hole Cover 1-3/4"

FOR BLINDS AND DOORS NAME THIS WAY: 59x36 2 inch faux wood blinds

DO NOT NAME THIS WAY: Blinds 59X36X2" Faux Wood

Description

Use this field for brands, colors, details, ratings, etc.

Add the link to order the part from the supplier in the description. Use the description field for the LINK to the part to order the part. Copy/paste the URL directly from the supplier. Use a link shortener website to shorten it like this one: [https://surl.li/wzrloa](https://surl.li/wzrloa)

Category

Be very consistent here when selecting the category. Techs need to be able to search by category.

Review the available categories as is. Do not excessively add new categories. [Inventory Categories](https://metricpropertymanagement.appfolio.com/maintenance/inventory_management/categories)

Part Number

Part number should exactly match the part number on the supplier website. Part number is also listed ON the box the inventory is kept in or labelled on the shelf the inventory item is kept on. For small items, the part number can be printed with the label maker and put on the item like a sticker.

Supplier

The supplier the part came from is very important.

If we have the same part from two different suppliers, the maintenance coordinator needs to decide which supplier ongoing we will purchase the part from, then the part number and supplier (and PRICE) should match the supplier we will use for this part ongoing.

Every inventory item needs a supplier. We generally use Amazon, Home Depot Pro, Home Depot Store, Ferguson. We can use one-off suppliers as needed as long as we are not duplicating parts.

Quantity

This is the exact number on hand at all times. Quantity is added when a part is ordered to start. Quantity is automatically updated as parts are used on work orders. Quantity that is manually updated during inventory checks means there is shrinkage (loss) and parts are being taken without being associated with a work order. This is a substantial loss.

Reorder

This is the threshold that you want the system to alert you at when it is time to reorder. The maintenance coordinator needs to decide the reorder number. Example- 10 toilet flappers are purchased and added to inventory with a reorder number of 5. A month later numerous work orders are completed and 5 flappers are used in work orders. The quantity would then be 5 flappers on hand. The reorder report would generate with flappers on the list as need to order. Reorder number makes it easy to place orders.

Cost

This is the actual cost WITH TAX per item. This is very important.

**DONT FORGET TO ADD THE TAX IN OR METRIC LOSES 8.25% ON EVERY PART**

- You must calculate the cost WITH TAX, therefore if the flapper is $9.99 each plus tax you calculate $9.99 X .0825 (the tax rate) and the cost is $10.81 each. If you skip the tax we lost 8.25% on every item (ouch).
- You must calculate the PER ITEM price. For instance, if you buy 10 flappers in a package and it is $99.99 for the 10 pack, calculate the cost per item. $9.99 divided by 10 = $9.99. Don't forget to add the tax!
- In the description always make note of items purchased in packages. For instance say "purchased in packages of 10 but used/sold per item"

Markup

Most markups are 25%. Make sure to choose percent, not fixed rate.

Exceptions are Equipment Rental which will be covered later.

Exceptions are very expensive HVAC parts where the maintenance coordinator may choose to do a lower markup.

Expense Account

This is the expense account on the property side that you want to hit the property expenses. It is usually close to the category name. If any doubt ask maintenance coordinator.

Storage Details

Where is this item stored specifically in the shop so it can be found easily. This is usually the same as the category.

Bin/Shelf Number

We use this field to list the unique URL for the inventory item. When creating an inventory item get all data saved then click "Save". Go to the URL and copy the URL. Edit the inventory item and paste the URL in the Bin/Shelf Number field and save again.

We use this for custom reporting to create unique URLs for inventory that are on each bin or shelf and help maintenance find the item in Appfolio easier.

records.fullText:
# Maintenance Property Inspection & Damage Reporting Policy

## Purpose

The purpose of this policy is to ensure that all properties are consistently monitored for visible damage, safety concerns, and maintenance needs. Maintenance Technicians serve as the **eyes and ears of the property** and play a critical role in identifying issues early to protect asset value, resident safety, and curb appeal.

## Scope

This policy applies to **all Maintenance Technicians** performing groundskeeping, turns, preventive maintenance, or regular repair work at any managed property.

## Policy Statement

Maintenance Technicians are required to **visibly inspect each property** while performing grounds duties or regular maintenance tasks. Any observed damage, safety concern, or maintenance issue that cannot be corrected immediately must be **reported promptly** using the approved reporting process.

Maintenance staff have a **duty to observe, document, and report** conditions that may require repair—even if the issue falls outside the scope of the technician’s assigned work for the day.

## Technician Responsibilities

While on-site, Maintenance Technicians must:

- Conduct a **visual inspection** of the property, including but not limited to:
    - Buildings, siding, roofs (from the ground)
    - Fencing, gates, and signage
    - Parking lots, sidewalks, and common areas
    - Exterior lighting
    - Visible plumbing, electrical, or HVAC concerns
    - Evidence of vandalism, water damage, or safety hazards
- **Address minor issues immediately** when possible and safe to do so.
- **Report any damage or required repairs** that cannot be resolved immediately.
- Understand that identifying and reporting issues is a core job responsibility, not optional.

## Reporting Process

If a technician observes damage or a repair need that cannot be completed right away:

1. **Take clear photos** of the issue from one or more angles.
1. **Post the photos** in the designated **Maintenance WhatsApp Channel.**
1. Include a brief description with:
    - Property name
    - Specific location (e.g., building number, unit number, or area)
    - Nature of the issue (e.g., water damage, broken fixture, safety concern)

**Example Post:**

_Property: Oak Ridge Apartments_

_Location: Building 3 – Rear Stairwell_

_Issue: Broken handrail – safety concern_

## Maintenance Coordinator Responsibilities

The Maintenance Coordinator will:

- **Monitor the Maintenance WhatsApp channel daily**.
- Review reported issues for completeness and urgency.
- **Create and assign service requests** for all ongoing or follow-up repairs.
- Prioritize repairs based on safety, liability, and operational impact.
- Track repeat or unresolved issues as part of preventive maintenance oversight.

## Accountability

- Failure to report visible property damage or maintenance needs may result in corrective action.
- Recognizing and reporting issues is considered part of professional maintenance standards and performance expectations.
- Consistent reporting supports proactive maintenance, reduces emergency repairs, and protects the company’s assets.

## Key Principle

Maintenance Technicians are the **first line of visibility** on each property. If you see something that looks wrong, unsafe, or damaged—**it must be reported**.

_If it’s visible to you, it matters to the property._

**Adding Inventory Upon Receipt**

All material purchased should be IMMEDIATELY added into inventory and should be checked out as needed by the technician (not end of day, not next day, not a text to the GM or a text to the inventory manager, nor a post-it).

The person receiving the materials (with the shipping slip or receipt/ invoice in their hand) should either:

A) PREFERRED: Immediately stock the inventory onto the shelves and write the material location on the invoice then scan it to metricpropertymanagement@proper.ai - make sure to note "Please add to inventory AND process this MPM Expense. This is an inventory item and is NOT Billable at this time"

B) ALTERNATIVELY: Store the items in the receiving area and write the material location "Receiving" then scan the invoice to metricpropertymanagement@proper.ai - make sure to note "Please add to inventory AND process this MPM Expense. This is an inventory item and is NOT Billable at this time"

Inventory Location Unknown: Use the "**RECEIVING**" location if the location is unknown. The inventory will be moved and location updated later. The important thing is to add the item(s) to inventory immediately.

Note for Operations Team- the inventory location has to be updated in Appfolio when it inventory is put away- otherwise inventory will be very hard to complete and techs cannot find the parts they need. Make a follow up task if needed. Do not leave items in "Receiving" location in Appfolio indefinitely.

All materials entered into inventory are subject to a 20% upcharge. If adding an item to inventory for the first time (new items), select the appropriate upcharge 20%, 25% or 0%.

**Property Owned Materials:**

Any materials purchased by the property, from the property bank account (this should be extremely rare) will be entered into inventory like all other materials and will be a ZERO percent markup. The materials will be stored on the shelf marked and designated specifically for that property or inventory stickers with the property name will be used to mark the inventory paid and owned by the property. This must be done immediately upon receipt so as not to mix up the inventory. The materials will be checked out and utilized like all other inventory otherwise. Note, Metric is not able to store materials for properties and should not be in the habit of storing materials for properties. Purchasing materials from the property's operating account and storing them in the warehouse should not be our daily practice.

Converting Invoices with Inventory Used:

If converting a work order to an invoice that includes a part (an inventory item) it is NOT necessary to add a markup! This is important: The markup is ALREADY ADDED in the Smart Bill settings as long as the item was properly entered into inventory upon receipt. Do not add a markup when converting ready to bill work orders to invoices.

All properties with gas must have a professionally printed sign posted in a common area that explains to residents that they should call emergency maintenance if they smell gas.

Reports of gas smell should be treated like a MAJOR emergency and handled immediately. These requests MUST be answered within an hour, around the clock, without fail.

All staff must be made aware that under no circumstance are they to report gas leaks to the gas company or the city unless they are directed to do so by a licensed plumber or ownership.

In the event that a resident reports a suspected gas leak to the gas company or city before reporting the suspected leak to maintenance or maintenance, the gas company will very likely shut off the gas to the property and require that the property be pressure tested fully before gas service is restored.

In this instance, immediately STOP and call Lyndsay Hanes at 512-986-9669 (cell) or Rebekah Tuckner at 512-563-1668. Either of these people will review the gas response plan depending on the situation. Do not call a plumber or discuss with the city of gas company further until you have reported the situation to the appropriate parties.

Reporting gas leaks according to this policy will reduce potentially extreme expenses, reduce downtime for repairs, and reduce the risk of negative publicity.

All new employees should be made aware of this policy before they work on a property.

records.title: Vacant Unit Energy Conservation Policy
records.fullText:
Purpose / Propósito

This policy ensures that vacant or make-ready apartments are managed in a way that conserves energy, reduces operating costs, and maintains equipment efficiency.

Esta política garantiza que los apartamentos vacantes o en proceso de preparación se gestionen de manera que se conserve energía, se reduzcan los costos operativos y se mantenga la eficiencia del equipo.

Scope / Alcance

This applies to all maintenance technicians, vendors, and staff who enter and service vacant or make-ready apartments.

Esto aplica a todos los técnicos de mantenimiento, proveedores y personal que ingresen y trabajen en apartamentos vacantes o en proceso de preparación.

**Policy / Política**

1. Lights / Luces

- All lights inside the apartment must be turned off at the end of each workday.
- Todas las luces dentro del apartamento deben apagarse al final de cada jornada laboral.
- Closet, bathroom, and appliance lights must not be left on unless specifically required for ongoing work.
- No se deben dejar encendidas las luces de clósets, baños o electrodomésticos, a menos que sean necesarias para el trabajo en curso.
- Remember: You might not return to that unit the same day. If you leave, turn off all lights before exiting.
- Recuerde: Puede que no regrese a esta unidad el mismo día. Si se va, apague todas las luces antes de salir.
- Think about it this way: if you were going out of town for a week, would you leave all the lights on in your house? Probably not—you’d take one minute to turn them off.
- Piénselo así: si se fuera de viaje por una semana, ¿dejaría todas las luces encendidas en su casa? Probablemente no—tomaría un minuto para apagarlas.

2. Air Conditioning & Heating / Aire Acondicionado y Calefacción

- Thermostats must be turned off in units that are vacant and not actively being shown.
- Los termostatos deben estar apagados en unidades vacantes que no estén siendo mostradas activamente.
- During make-ready, if climate control is needed (e.g., for paint curing, humidity control, or extreme weather), thermostats must be set to 78°F cooling in summer or 65°F heating in winter.
- Durante el proceso de preparación, si se necesita control de clima (por ejemplo, para secado de pintura, control de humedad o clima extremo), los termostatos deben ajustarse a 78°F para enfriar en verano o 65°F para calentar en invierno.
- If you leave the unit—even if you think you’ll return later—set the thermostat to off.
- Si se va de la unidad—even si cree que volverá más tarde—ajuste el termostato a apagado.
- Think of it like your own home: if you were leaving for the day or a trip, you’d adjust the thermostat to save money and protect your system.
- Piénselo como su propia casa: si se fuera por el día o de viaje, ajustaría el termostato para ahorrar dinero y proteger su sistema.

3. Cost Impact / Impacto de Costos

- A single one-bedroom apartment left with all lights on and the thermostat set extremely low can cost our clients hundreds of dollars per month in wasted utilities.
- Un apartamento de una habitación con todas las luces encendidas y el termostato muy bajo puede costar a nuestros clientes cientos de dólares al mes en servicios desperdiciados.
- Wasting electricity = wasting money. We have a duty to our clients to be good stewards of their money, and that means treating each vacant unit as if it were our own home and our own utility bill.
- Desperdiciar electricidad = desperdiciar dinero. Tenemos el deber con nuestros clientes de ser buenos administradores de su dinero, y eso significa tratar cada unidad vacante como si fuera nuestro propio hogar y nuestra propia factura de servicios.

4. Accountability & Policy Adherence / Responsabilidad y Cumplimiento de la Política

- The last technician or vendor leaving a unit is responsible for ensuring compliance.
- El último técnico o proveedor que salga de una unidad es responsable de asegurar el cumplimiento.
- Specifically, the last technician with time accumulated in the system for that apartment will be held responsible for any breach of this policy.
- Específicamente, el último técnico con tiempo registrado en el sistema para esa unidad será responsable de cualquier incumplimiento de esta política.
- Supervisors will perform random inspections to confirm policy adherence.
- Los supervisores realizarán inspecciones aleatorias para confirmar el cumplimiento de la política.
- Failure to follow this policy may result in a written warning and/or retraining.
- No seguir esta política puede resultar en una advertencia por escrito y/o reentrenamiento.

Benefits / Beneficios

- Conserves energy and reduces utility expenses.
- Conserva energía y reduce gastos de servicios.
- Extends the life of HVAC systems.
- Extiende la vida útil de los sistemas de HVAC.
- Promotes responsibility and professionalism among staff.
- Promueve responsabilidad y profesionalismo entre el personal.
- Protects client relationships and property value.
- Protege la relación con los clientes y el valor de la propiedad.
- Demonstrates stewardship of client resources.
- Demuestra administración responsable de los recursos del cliente.

records.fullText:
Esta Política de Mantenimiento establece las expectativas y responsabilidades de todo el personal de mantenimiento para garantizar operaciones eficientes, la finalización puntual de las tareas y una comunicación adecuada. Cumplir con estos estándares es esencial para mantener la calidad y seguridad de nuestras propiedades.

---

### 1. Finalización de Órdenes de Trabajo

- Todo el personal de mantenimiento debe completar las órdenes de trabajo asignadas a través del sistema designado en AppFolio.
- No se permite la discreción personal en la priorización de tareas o la desviación de las órdenes asignadas a menos que sea aprobado explícitamente por un supervisor.
- Cualquier solicitud verbal o informal de los residentes debe documentarse y añadirse al sistema de órdenes de trabajo antes de su ejecución.

---

### 2. Puntualidad y Registro de Horas

- Todo el personal de mantenimiento debe presentarse a trabajar a tiempo según los horarios asignados.
- Está estrictamente prohibido registrar la salida antes del horario programado sin la aprobación previa de un supervisor.
- Los retrasos habituales o las salidas anticipadas sin permiso resultarán en medidas disciplinarias que pueden incluir el despido.

---

### 3. Comunicación

- El personal de mantenimiento debe responder a los mensajes de su supervisor dentro de los **10 minutos** posteriores a ser contactados durante el horario laboral.
- No responder dentro de este período en **dos ocasiones separadas** resultará en la terminación inmediata del empleo.
- El personal debe asegurarse de que sus teléfonos o dispositivos de comunicación estén operativos y accesibles durante las horas laborales.

---

### 4. Conducta Profesional

- Se espera que todo el personal demuestre profesionalismo y respeto al interactuar con los residentes, supervisores y compañeros de trabajo.
- No se tolerará ninguna forma de comportamiento poco profesional, negligencia en las tareas o insubordinación.

---

### 5. Responsabilidad y Cumplimiento

- Se realizarán auditorías regulares para garantizar la finalización de las órdenes de trabajo y el cumplimiento de esta política.
- Los supervisores revisarán los registros de horario, el estado de las órdenes de trabajo y los registros de comunicación para evaluar el desempeño.
- Las violaciones a esta política resultarán en acciones correctivas inmediatas, incluidas advertencias, suspensiones o terminación, dependiendo de la gravedad y frecuencia de la infracción.

---

    - Verbal requests for tasks not entered into the system must be added as service requests by the maintenance staff before the task is completed. Service team members should ask the resident, or office team member, to place the service request via the Maintenance Hotline, resident portal, or for office team members, via Appfolio directly.

records.title: Time Tracking & Payment Standards for 1099 Contractors
records.fullText:
Individuals that work for Metric Property Management on a contract basis are paid based on work completed and are classified as 1099 contractors. All work has to be properly documented, completed fully, and completed in an industry acceptable timeframe in order to be eligible for payment.

Invoices for 1099 contractors are created based on verified, complete, quality work documented in Appfolio _ONLY._ Any work completed that is not fully complete with full documentation is not eligible to be invoiced and paid.

# SERVICE REQUEST REQUIRED FOR ALL WORK/SERVICE REQUESTS

- All work must be completed with an associated work order in Appfolio. Any contractor can add their own service requests directly into Appfolio. Any contractor that is asked by a supervisor or a team member to complete work without a work order should politely ask whomever assigned them the work to give them a service request or they should enter the service request themselves. Absolutely no work is to be completed without a service request. 

# PROGRESS AND COMPLETION NOTES REQUIRED FOR ALL SERVICE REQUESTS

- Every single service request requires notes regarding the completion from beginning to end of the service request. 
    - Example: 4/9 looked at garbage disposal- needs replacement. Ordering today will be back Tuesday to install. 4/11 replaced garbage disposal. 
    - Example: Grounds completed- need a follow up work order for pool pump. 
    - Example: Knocked on door but deadbolt was locked so could not enter. 

# PHOTOS ARE REQUIRED FOR ALL SERVICE REQUESTS

- Every single service request required a photo (or more if necessary) to document the start and end of the service request fully. The photos should leave zero doubt what was completed in the home. 
- The tech MUST USE a GPS and time stamp app for ALL which are available for free in the Apple Store [Apple Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/gps-camera-55-field-survey/id1439730560) and Play Store [Play Store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=gpsmapcamera.locationonphoto.geotag.gpscamera&hl=en_US) and works for both Android and iPhone users. Photos without a time/GPS stamp are not accepted. 

# START AND STOP TIMES REQUIRED FOR ALL SERVICE REQUESTS/WORK

- All service requests must be fully documented with the actual start and stop times within the work order in Appfolio for each and every minute the contractor is working on the service request. 
    - Example: A service request to unclog a toilet is placed. The contractor will "start" the clock on the service request when they head to the property. They easily fix the clog, make notes in the service request and attach photo documentation, and they will "stop" the clock on the service request when they finish the documentation then they will complete the service request. 
    - Example: On Mondays a service request for grounds keeping is assigned to the contractor for Oak Tree Apartments. This service request specifically states it is for the week. The start and stop times need to be documented each and every time the contractor is working on grounds on Oak Tree Apartments. There may be 3 entries for the week or there may be 10. Every single minute of groundskeeping completed during the week must be clocked in the service requests in Appfolio. 
    - Example: A service request for a garbage disposal clogged is placed. The contractor should "start" the clock on the service request the moment they head to the property. They arrive and discover that they need a replacement disposal, which they do not have on stock. They will either order the part or notify the Maintenance Coordinator that they need a garbage disposal. They will then "stop" the clock on the service request and go to the next service request. When the garbage disposal arrives, they will "start" the clock on the service request, go replace the garbage disposal, then "stop" the clock after submitting all documentation, then complete the service request in Appfolio. There will be two billable times for that one service request in Appfolio. 
- It is possible to edit start and stop times but it is highly discourated and closely monitored. An edited start and stop time should be a last resort and should be few and far in between. Actual clock in/out is required 95% of the time and failure to accurately use the start/stop feature can and will result in refusal of billing eligible hours. 

# QUALITY CONTROL

- Our clients expect repairs to be completed correctly the first time. We may refuse billing for unnecessary "call backs" for low quality work. 
- Time management is crucial. The Maintenance Coordinator closely monitors work order completion and compares the time it takes on service request to normal industry standards to be sure we are billing our clients fairly. If a job should take 2 hours and it takes 8, there will be a stern discussion the first time, then a potential dock in pay or severance of contract for repeated wasted client time. 

# BILLING ELIGIBLE

- Work must be completed to be billed
- Work is audited for accuracy
- Surveys are sent to every resident when service requests are completed and positive reviews are expected on every service request
- Work is audited for industry acceptable completion times
- Actual start and stop times are required on every service request
- Progress and completion notes are required on every service request
- Progress and completion photos are required on every service request

SERVICE REQUESTS CANNOT BE BILLED OUT WITHOUT ACCURATE START/END TIMES, PROGRESS NOTES, COMPLETION NOTES, PROGRESS PHOTOS AND COMPLETION PHOTOS - THEREFORE, WITHOUT THESE ITEMS THE SERVICE REQUEST IS NOT BILLABLE.

# ADHERENCE

1st warning - Failure to Provide Photos/Completion Notes: Failure to adhere to the above policy for service completion notes and photos will result in the contractor being asked to come to the office and personally update all of the completed work orders for the billing period. Failure to do so will result in delays in pay or potentially reduction of pay.

records.fullText:
**Before Messaging Your Boss (a.k.a. the IT Department)**

Let’s be honest — losing your RingCentral password happens to everyone eventually.

Your first instinct might be:

“I’ll just ask my boss; they’ll know what to do.”

But in our case, the boss is IT, and that means you’ve now handed them a task you could probably solve in five minutes yourself. It’s not just about saving them time — it’s about keeping things moving without waiting in line for help.

Here’s how to handle it like a pro 👇

**🧭 Step 1: Try the Reset Link**

Head to the RingCentral login page → click “Forgot Password”

Follow the prompts to send yourself a reset email.

- Check spam/junk folders.
- Verify you’re using the correct login email.
- Search your inbox for “RingCentral password reset.”

✅ If the reset email comes through — fix complete.

❌ If not, move to Step 2.

**🗂️ Step 2: Look for Saved Passwords**

Before escalating, check the places where passwords hide:

- Browser password manager: Chrome → Settings → Passwords → “RingCentral.”
- Password app (1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass, etc.).
- Old onboarding or setup docs — sometimes credentials live there.

Found it? Log in, celebrate your independence, and move on with your day.

**📬 Step 3: Search Old Emails**

Look up your original RingCentral welcome or setup emails.

They often contain your username and a direct password-reset link.

**🧑‍💻 Step 4: If You Have Admin Access**

If you happen to have admin permissions:

1. Log in at [service.ringcentral.com](https://service.ringcentral.com/).
1. Go to Users → [Your Name] → Reset Password.
1. Send the reset email to yourself.

(If you’re not an admin, skip this step — no need to poke around where you shouldn’t.)

**💡 Step 5: Contact IT (a.k.a. the Boss,**

**the Last Resort**

**)**

If nothing’s worked so far, then it’s time to reach out.

When you do, make it clear you’ve already tried to fix it yourself — it helps them help you faster and shows you respect their time.

Here’s what to say:

Subject: RingCentral Login – Password Reset Request

Hi [Boss’s Name],

I’m unable to log in to my RingCentral account ([username or extension]). I’ve already tried:

• “Forgot Password” link (no reset email received)

• Checked spam/junk folders

• Looked for saved passwords in my browser and manager

• Searched onboarding/setup emails

Could you please help by sending a reset link or unlocking my login?

Thanks!

[Your Name]

**🚫 Why This Matters**

Every time we skip these steps, it turns into a game of “Boss Ping-Pong” — you message them, they open IT, IT sends you a reset, and you wait.

But when you try the basics first, you usually fix it yourself — and you show you’re capable, resourceful, and respectful of everyone’s time.

**🧠 Pro Tips for Next Time**

- Store your new password in your password manager.
- Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA).
- Bookmark the login and password reset pages.
- Save this guide somewhere visible — your future self will thank you.

Would you like me to format this as a branded one-pager (for internal posting or onboarding) — maybe with your company name and a header graphic — so it looks official and easy to share?

records.title: Connecting AppFolio Reports to Microsoft Excel
records.fullText:
## Overview

The **AppFolio Report Connection** allows you to connect AppFolio reports directly to Microsoft Excel. Instead of manually exporting reports each time, you can refresh the data in Excel to retrieve the latest information from AppFolio while preserving your formulas, pivot tables, charts, and dashboards.

This is especially useful for recurring operational, accounting, leasing, and portfolio reporting.

---

# Benefits

- Eliminate repetitive CSV exports
- Refresh reports with one click
- Keep dashboards automatically updated
- Preserve formulas, PivotTables, charts, and formatting
- Reduce manual reporting errors
- Save time on weekly and monthly reporting

---

# Requirements

Before you begin, ensure you have:

- AppFolio account with permission to access reports
- Microsoft Excel (Microsoft 365 or Excel 2019+ recommended)
- AppFolio Report Connection installed
- Internet connection
- Active AppFolio login

---

# Connecting a Report

### Step 1

Open Microsoft Excel.

### Step 2A

Go to the **Home** tab.

**Step 2B**

Click Add-ins and loo for **AppFolio Report Connection** option.

[IMAGE]

### Step 3

Click **AppFolio Report Connection**.

[IMAGE]

### Step 4

Sign in using your AppFolio credentials if prompted.

### Step 5

Select the desired AppFolio database.

[IMAGE]

### Step 6

Choose the saved report you want to connect/import.

[IMAGE]

[IMAGE]

Examples:

- Rent Roll
- Delinquency Report
- Property Directory
- Leasing Activity
- Owner Statement
- Unit Directory
- Tenant Directory
- Work Orders
- Vendor Directory

### Step 7

Configure report filters.

Examples include:

- Property
- Date Range
- Status
- Unit Type
- Owner
- Custom Report Filters

### Step 8

Click **Load**.

The report data will populate directly into Excel.

---

# Refreshing Data

Whenever you need updated information:

1. Select Refresh in the **AppFolio Report Connection**.
1. Click **Refresh This Sheet /** **Refresh All**.

[IMAGE]

Excel will reconnect to AppFolio and retrieve the latest report data.

Any PivotTables, formulas, charts, or dashboards linked to the table will update after refreshing (you may also need to refresh PivotTables if they are not configured to update automatically).

---

# Best Practices

- Keep one worksheet dedicated to the raw AppFolio data.
- Avoid editing the imported data directly.
- Add calculations using separate columns or additional worksheets.
- Use named tables when creating formulas.
- Refresh data before distributing reports.
- Save the workbook after each successful refresh.

---

# Common Issues

## Login Prompt Appears Repeatedly

**Possible Causes**

- Session expired
- Password changed
- Multi-factor authentication required

**Resolution**

- Sign in again.
- Complete MFA if prompted.
- Restart Excel if the issue persists.

---

## Refresh Failed

**Possible Causes**

- Internet connection lost
- AppFolio unavailable
- Report permissions changed

**Resolution**

- Verify internet connectivity.
- Confirm the report still exists in AppFolio.
- Check that you still have permission to access the report.
- Retry the refresh.

---

## Report Loads Slowly

Large reports may take several minutes to load.

**Recommendations**

- Filter by property when possible.
- Limit date ranges.
- Remove unnecessary columns.
- Refresh during off-peak hours if working with very large datasets.

---

## Missing Data

Check that:

- Report filters are correct.
- The selected property is included.
- The date range is correct.
- The report contains records in AppFolio.

---

# Recommended Workflow

1. Open the Excel reporting workbook.
1. Click  **AppFolio Report Connection → Refresh All**.
1. Wait for the AppFolio report to finish loading.
1. Save the workbook.
1. Share or distribute the updated report.

---

# Example Use Cases

| Report | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Rent Roll | Occupancy and rental income reporting |
| Delinquency Report | Collections monitoring |
| Leasing Activity | Weekly leasing performance |
| Unit Directory | Unit availability tracking |
| Property Directory | Portfolio overview |
| Work Orders | Maintenance reporting |
| Owner Statement | Owner financial reporting |
| Tenant Directory | Resident management |

---

# Tips

- Refresh reports before meetings to ensure current data.
- Maintain a consistent workbook structure so dashboards continue to function after refreshes.
- Avoid renaming or deleting the imported data table unless you plan to recreate the connection.
- For large portfolios, consider separate workbooks by region or property group to improve performance.

---

# Support

If you encounter issues with the AppFolio Report Connection:

1. Verify your AppFolio permissions.
1. Restart Excel.
1. Re-authenticate your AppFolio account.
1. Reinstall the AppFolio Report Connection if the Excel add-in is missing.
1. Contact your AppFolio administrator or AppFolio Support if the issue persists.
