**Purpose**

To ensure **100% of rental applications** in AppFolio are processed **consistently, completely, and the same day**, with all documentation attached, verifications requested, and follow-ups executed on a defined cadence.

---

**Scope**

This SOP applies to **all rental applications** in AppFolio, including:

- Newly received applications
- Pending or partially processed applications
- Previously approved applications requiring documentation
- Incomplete or unpaid applications

---

Add these activities immediately with due date today:

- Confirm app fee paid. If not paid, send resident text. Complete when app fee is paid. Continue to text and call resident daily for 3 days. On day 4 message assigned leasing agent or property manager and advise that application will be denied tomorrow if app fee not paid and ask them to reach out to applicant ASAP. 
- Confirm either 4 pay stubs or 3 months bank statements attached. Check pay stub amounts to confirm 3X rent. Check check dates and accuracy. Check bank statement deposits. Confirm attached to Appfolio and labelled. 
- Confirm all of this with tenant by sending a text: We wanted to let you know we received your application and wills start working on it. I may have a few follow up questions. For now can you please confirm that the follow people are the ONLY people that will be living in the apartment? If there is anyone else, including other adults or children or pets that need to be added, please update your application via the application portal. (List names)
- Send work verification via Appfolio if employed. Appfolio usually automatically sends it but if not, send it manually. 
- Send rental verification if renting from apartment. Appfolio usually automatically sends it but if not, send it manually. 
- Run credit AFTER app fee paid, all applicants are on application (adults). Wait to collect app fee and have all applicants before screening. 
- Review screening. Send rental verification for any hidden landlords at apartment communities manually. Check for broken leases, landlord debt. If addresses exist to apartments not listed on application, send a manual rental history request via email and attach to profile. 

**Resources: Application Processing Checklist**

[https://netorgft5473895-my.sharepoint.com/:w:/g/personal/lyndsay_metricpropertymanagement_com/IQB3rdRAZwqOQYodim1e6EHUASdbWHs4JUutpi0fFxM0CDw](https://netorgft5473895-my.sharepoint.com/:w:/g/personal/lyndsay_metricpropertymanagement_com/IQB3rdRAZwqOQYodim1e6EHUASdbWHs4JUutpi0fFxM0CDw)

**Definitions**

**Fully Processed Application (Required Standard)**

An application is considered **fully processed** only when **all requirements below are complete, documented, and auditable**.

---

**Processing Requirements**

**1. Income Documentation and Review**

- At least **one (1) full month of verifiable income** is required.
- **Every income source listed** must have **recent supporting documentation**.
- All income documentation must be:
    - Attached to the **tenant profile**
    - Clearly named and auditable

**Documentation Notes (Required):**

A note must be added to the tenant profile confirming review and qualification.

Example:

“Pay stubs reviewed: one full month provided, legitimacy confirmed, income exceeds 3x rent.”

If income documentation is insufficient:

- Contact the applicant immediately
- Create an activity for the missing item
- Follow the standard follow-up cadence

---

**2. Photo Identification**

- **Photo ID is required for every applicant age 18+**
- IDs must be:
    - Attached to the tenant profile
    - Clearly named

---

**3. Application Fee Status**

- **Application fees must be collected for all applicants age 18+.**
- If unpaid:
    - Begin fee follow-up immediately
    - **Do not process credit screening**
    - You may continue to request and review income, rental, and ID documentation

---

**4. Verification Requests (Sent via AppFolio)**

- **Employment verification** is required for employed applicants
- **Rental history verification** is required for all applicable landlords
- All verification requests must be sent through the **AppFolio profile** whenever possible

If AppFolio cannot resend a rental history request:

- Email the verification directly to the landlord
- Create and track an activity in the tenant profile
- 

**Approval Considerations**

- Lack of a response from an employer or landlord is not, by itself, grounds for denial.
- If sufficient supporting documentation exists, such as bank statements showing consistent income deposits and regular rent payments, the application may continue to be evaluated based on the totality of the information provided.
- Rental payment history evidenced through bank statements may be used to support rental history when landlord verification is unavailable.
- The goal is to verify the applicant's ability to pay and rental performance using all available documentation, not solely third-party responses.

---

**5. Follow-Up Cadence (Required for All Missing Items)**

This cadence applies to **fees, income documents, IDs, verifications, and landlord responses**.

- **Day 1:** Text the applicant via AppFolio
- **Day 2:** Call and text the applicant (document call in notes)
- **Day 3:** Text the applicant and assign the leasing agent a task to call
- **Day 4:** If no compliance, **cancel the application** and document in profile notes

---

**6. Activities (Non-Negotiable)**

- **Every missing or pending item must have an activity** in the tenant profile
- Activities must be:
    - Assigned to the processor
    - Worked **daily** until resolved or cancelled

There is **no reason to re-review an application from the beginning**:

- Fully review upon receipt
- Create activities for all outstanding items
- Work exclusively from the activity list

---

**Step-by-Step Procedure**

---

**Step 1: Intake and Initial Review (Same Day)**

1. Open the application immediately upon receipt.
1. Confirm application fee status for all applicants age 18+.
    - If unpaid: begin fee follow-up. Do not process credit screening.
1. Create activities for **every missing item**, including but not limited to:
    - Missing fees
    - Missing IDs
    - Missing income documentation
    - Missing landlord or employer information
1. Attach all received documents to the tenant profile immediately.

**Example Activity Notes:**

- “Second pay stub missing — text sent via AppFolio, pending receipt.”
- “Social Security income verification missing — follow-up sent.”
- “Application fee unpaid for co-applicant — fee follow-up initiated.”

---

**Step 2: Income Verification Standards**

**Minimum Requirement**

- One full month of verifiable income must be documented.

Self-employed or cash-paid applicants:

- Employer letter (if available)
- **Three months of bank statements required**

---

**Acceptable Documentation**

**Employed Applicants**

- Recent pay stubs covering at least one full month
- Must show:
    - Applicant name
    - Employer name
    - Pay dates and amounts
- Employer must match application
- Pay dates and check numbers must align

**Self-Employed or Cash Income**

- Verification letter confirming income source
- Three months of bank statements showing:
    - Consistent income deposits
    - Rent payments to a landlord

**Other Income Sources**

- Child support
- Pension
- Social Security
- Any additional income listed

Each income source requires **recent proof** and a review note.

---

**Step 3: Employment Verification**

1. Send employment verification via AppFolio.
1. Confirm submission in the Activity Log.
1. Create an activity to track completion.

If no employer response:

- Continue using tenant-provided income documentation
- Employment verification is supplemental, not the sole approval factor

---

**Step 4: Rental History Verification**

1. Review the credit screening report.
1. Compare addresses to those listed on the application.

**Listed Rental History**

- Send verification through AppFolio.

**Undisclosed Rental History (Heightened Risk)**

- Treat as potential intentional non-disclosure
- Send verification for undisclosed addresses:
    - Via AppFolio if possible
    - Via email if AppFolio cannot send
- Create and track an activity until resolved

**When Rental History Is Not Required (Rare)**

- Applicant has never rented **and**
- No rental addresses appear on the credit report

If an address appears on the credit report:

- Research it (e.g., Google)
- If it appears to be a rental, send verification
- 

**Approval Considerations (Bekah)**

- Lack of a response from an employer or landlord is not, by itself, grounds for denial.
- If sufficient supporting documentation exists, such as bank statements showing consistent income deposits and regular rent payments, the application may continue to be evaluated based on the totality of the information provided.
- Rental payment history evidenced through bank statements may be used to support rental history when landlord verification is unavailable.
- The goal is to verify the applicant's ability to pay and rental performance using all available documentation, not solely third-party responses.
- 

---

**Step 5: Activity Log Review**

Use the AppFolio Activity Log to confirm:

- Employment verification sent
- Rental history verification sent

Additional guidance:

- AppFolio automatically resends requests
- Lack of response alone is not grounds for denial
- Undisclosed rental history requires priority follow-up

---

**Step 6: Application Fee Follow-Up**

Applications are **not processed** until all fees are paid.

**Fee Follow-Up Cadence**

- Day 1: Text applicant
- Day 2: Call and text
- Day 3: Text, call, and assign leasing agent task
- Day 4: Cancel application

An activity must remain open until paid or cancelled.

---

**Step 7: Run the Screening**

Run the screening only if the application fee has been paid.

- While we often say “running the credit report,” the process in AppFolio actually includes both a **background check** and a **credit report**.

**Social Security Number Requirement:**

- If an applicant **does not have a Social Security Number (SSN)**, they will **not** have a credit report.
- In this case, **do not run the credit portion** of the check.

**AppFolio Settings:**

- A new setting allows you to choose whether to run:
    - **Background check + Credit report**
    - **Background check only**
- **Before pressing the “Screen” button**, check if any applicants have an SSN.
    - If **none** have an **** SSN → select **Background check only**.
    - If **any** have an SSN → select **Background check + Credit report**.

**Cost Efficiency:**

- Running the credit portion for applicants without SSNs is unnecessary and incurs extra cost.
- Always verify SSNs first to ensure cost-effective screening.

**Training:**

- All team members must watch the instructional video on this setting **today** to familiarize themselves with the updated process.

---

**Step 8: Missing Information Follow-Up**

For **every missing item**:

1. Create an activity assigned to yourself
1. Follow up daily
1. Use the standard Day 1–Day 4 cadence

No pending item may exist without an activity.

---

**Step 9: Same-Day Processing Standard**

All applications must be processed the **same day they are received**.

Processing includes:

- Fee review and follow-up
- Document review and attachment
- Verification requests sent
- Activities created for all outstanding items

---

**Accountability and Best Practices**

- Process applications immediately upon receipt
- Work exclusively from your AppFolio activity list
- Never rely on memory
- If something is missing, request it immediately and document the action
- Prioritize risk management, especially undisclosed rental history

**Goal:**

✅ Zero stalled applications

✅ Complete, auditable documentation on every file

## Application Processing – Daily Activities Reporting

**Purpose:**

To ensure all applications are processed consistently and all activities are tracked in AppFolio, with daily reporting for transparency and accountability.

---

### 1. Assign Activities to Applications

- Every new application automatically receives a standard set of activities in AppFolio (e.g., Initial Screening, Credit Check, Reference Call, Lease Document Preparation).
- Mark activities as **Completed** once done.
- Any activity not yet completed remains **Pending**.
- There should normally be only **2 pending activities per application category**, unless new applications are added.

---

### 2. Generate the Daily Activities Report

1. Log in to AppFolio.
1. Navigate to the **Activities Report**.
1. Ensure the report shows **both Completed and Pending activities**.
1. Take a **snippet of the top portion** (roughly fits one page) to include in your daily summary.

---

### 3. End-of-Day Summary

Prepare a summary with the following components:

**a) Application Status**

| Windy Hill 137 | Completed | 0 |
| Urban Villa 125 | Pending | 2 |

**d) Notes (Optional)**

- All new applications have been assigned standard activities.
- Pending items have been highlighted for completion tomorrow.
- Completed activities for today have been recorded in AppFolio.

---

### 4. Submission

- Submit the summary **before the end of the day**.
- Continue submitting this daily to demonstrate activity tracking and application progress.

---

### 5. Verification

- Anyone can open the **Activities tab** of an application in AppFolio to see exactly which activities are completed and which are pending.
- This ensures transparency and accountability across the team.

records.fullText:
**Email Management Playbook**

**1. Escalation Rules** - **** Always escalate to me:

- Anything with deadlines inside 48 hours
- Emails from ownership, asset managers, or corporate
- Legal, compliance, or money-related items
- If you’re unsure about an event/invitation:
    - Don’t decline or accept on my behalf.
    - Message me for approval, then archive it once I respond.

**2. Task & Follow-Up Handling** - **** If an email requires someone else’s action:

- Create a task in Asana.
- Assign it to the correct team member.
- Add the email context/details in the task notes.
- Once the task is created, move the email to Archive – Handled.
- If the task requires follow-up but isn’t urgent:
    - Track it in Asana under “_Waiting On_.”
    - No need to keep it in my inbox.

**3. Inbox Processing Workflow**

- _Morning Sweep (30 min):_ Review all new emails, escalate urgent ones, create Asana tasks, archive junk.
- _Midday Check (10 min):_ Quick scan for new urgent items.
- _End-of-Day Review (20 min):_ Make sure all escalations are sent, Asana is updated, and inbox is organized.

**4. Folder System**

- _Action_ – Bekah → Only what I must personally handle
    - Property walk-through – inspection walkthrough with the owner
    - All Types Payments processing
    - Liens – case potentially being filed by a vendor 
    - Owner’s email – emails addressed to her 
- _Action_ – Assistant → What you’re still working on
    - Owner’s email – Tasks which I can generate on Bekah’s behalf 
    - Team’s email 
        - Jaen – approval required
        - Maintenance email
        - Accounting Emails
        - Asana Tasks / Reminder
- _Waiting On_ → For reference until follow-up is received
- _Archive (Handled)_ → Everything closed out or logged

**5. Special Rule: Owner Emails**

- _Every owner response must be acknowledged the same day it is received._
- _Even if the full answer isn’t ready, reply with:_
    - “Hi [Owner Name], I’m working on this and will follow up with you once it’s completed / by [specific time or date].”
- _Task Tracking:_
    - Every owner-related email must also be added to the Owner Asana Board.
    - Assign to the correct team member or to me if it requires my action.

**6. Archiving Rule:**

- Only move the email to Archive – Handled when:
    - The task has been fully completed, or
    - It has been reassigned and accepted in Asana.
    - Do not archive owner emails right after acknowledgment — they stay open until there’s true follow-through.
    - This structure will make sure my inbox is always clear, nothing important gets missed, and owners always receive timely responses. Let’s use this as the standard going forward.

records.title: No Payments in Office Policy
records.fullText:
Metric leases all state that payments must be made on the resident portal or the resident is subject to a $50 convenience fee for payments made in office. There is a cash pay option for residents that is extremely easy to use. We should not be taking checks and money orders by mail or in office generally.

We will be auditing checks and money orders received in office monthly and reviewing this closely for performance with all employees involved. The person accepting the in-person payment AND the collections person who posted the payment has responsibility.

**EXCEPTIONS**

HOUSING PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS: We have no choice but to deviate from this policy for residents receiving assistance from housing assistance agencies (Housing Choice Voucher, Life Works, Caritas of Austin, etc.) If at ALL possible the agency should pay via ACH.

EVICTIONS: The collections team can take a large, lump sum payment in certified funds in exchange for dismissing a previously filed eviction.

MANAGEMENT APPROVAL: We commit to our clients that we will not "lose a resident" over the electronic payments policy. In 6 years of business we have allowed only 3 residents to pay "old school" regularly due to client request and tenure. This requires Rebekah or Lyndsay to approve. Don't count on it. We'll be calling the resident and convincing them to pay electronically, trust me.

WHAT TO DO WHEN A RESIDENT BRINGS A PAYMENT TO THE OFFICE

If a resident presents payment in office, politely remind the resident we require electronic payments and that our leases state there is a $50 convenience fee for payments made in office.

Do they have a check in hand? Hand them your computer and let them login go the portal to pay with their check info.

Do they have a money order in hand? Explain to them they need to return their money order to the place of purchase for a refund and send them the cash pay instructions.

Do they have cash in hand? Never, in ANY circumstances should you take cash. If an employee takes cash, even if they go purchase a money order for the resident or pay for the resident in any way, it is grounds for immediate termination. Hand their cash back and send them the cash pay instructions.

RESIDENTS ARE REQUIRED TO "SELF SERVE" WHENEVER POSSIBLE

DO NOT sign up for the portal for a resident. You can send them instructions to do so only. You cannot do it for them. Here's a guide for that: [Guide to Resident Portal Appfolio](https://metric.slab.com/posts/k7ujt29s)

DO NOT sign a resident up for cash pay. You can send them instructions to do so only. You cannot do it for them.

AGENCY PAYMENTS

Assistance agencies or housing authorities can make resident payments. Whomever is establishing this relationship should REALLY push for electronic payments. If those are not possible, payments should be mailed to PO Box 2043, Leander TX 78646. Here is the Metric w9: [https://acrobat.adobe.com/id/urn:aaid:sc:VA6C2:7eb1a518-c836-45e3-9fee-5b982206bbae](https://acrobat.adobe.com/id/urn:aaid:sc:VA6C2:7eb1a518-c836-45e3-9fee-5b982206bbae)

Property W9's are saved to the property documents in Appfolio.

Property Management Agreements are saved to OneDrive as well as the property documents in Appfolio. Email marketing@metricpropertymanagement.com for assistance if you need a copy of a PMA and have searched and cannot find it.

ACCOUNTING FOR AGENCY PAYMENTS

Our Accounting Team will post ALL resident payments, including agency payments made electronically or in person.

> **Our Accounting Team Does Not Know Our Residents Like We Do. Make Sure The Deposits Are Clean and Clear So That Someone Who Knows Zero History Will Have the Necessary Information to Post the Payment.** 

Our Accounting Team MUST have real-time updates on all payments made by agencies whether that is in-office or electronic. ACH payments made cannot be posted without the details.

The email address on file for ACH payment notification must be metricpropertymanagement@proper.ai

Do not add your email address or any other address. There is no reason to double the work. One email from the agency with notice of payments made and details should be sent to Accounting ONLY.

Any agency that has a portal to check logins must be shared with our Accounting Team. Do not update or change this login without also updating the Accounting Team! Email metricpropertymanagement@proper.ai the  following to them when setting up any new agency or assistance organization:

Property Name (one or all)

Resident Name

Portal URL

Portal Username

Portal Password

Payments received from agencies in office must be deposited SAME DAY via the check scanner. If it is a single resident payment, make sure the resident name and unit number are printed or written in the memo of the check prior to scanning. Hint- you can simply save the bank deposit from the banking portal and send that as long as the residents name/unit is on the check you deposited. If it is a multiple resident payment, the payment should have been sent with a remittance including the details. Make the bank deposit then scan and email the deposit to the Accounting Team.

One Deposit = One Email with all necessary info to post the payment(s) EXACTLY as they hit the bank account. DO NOT break these transactions up.

records.file: slab/Support/Procedures/How to File an Incident Report.md
records.title: Filing an Incident Report
records.fullText:
Incident reports are critical in an emergency situation to make sure all information is written down while it is still fresh. This will ensure the most accurate information is gathered, reported and documented for all injuries, property damage or crime related to the property

**Here are some dos and don'ts when it comes to Incident Reports.**

**Do's:**

1. Always FIRST call 911 if you have a true emergency. The safety of staff and residents is the most important. 
1. Call your supervisor as soon as you possibly can when there is any type of incident such as injuries, property damage or crime related to the property. 
- If you don't reach your supervisor, repeat attempts to reach them at least 3 times, then escalate to the Vice President of Property Management or Lyndsay Hanes.
1. Handle the emergency. Get police report numbers, get officer names, get details of what happened. Property Manager's should make every effort to quickly go to the property when a serious incident occurs. 
1. Immediately after handling the urgent situation, fill out an incident report with all information  and send to your direct supervisor via email along with [info@metricpropertymanagement.com](mailto:info@metricpropertymanagement.com)
1. As details come up, send an updated incident reports.

List of what constitutes an incident report:

- Fire
- Injury 
- Loss of Life
- Serious Floods
- Potential HR issues
- Vandalism
- Property Crime
- Damage to Property

Their are many more instances but when questioning 'Should I do a report or no?' it is always safer to send an incident report.

**Do Not's:**

- Don't wait until after the incident has completely been resolved to call your supervisor- notify your supervisor as soon as possible. 
- Don't call your supervisor before you call 911. 911 should be your first call if it is necessary and then you can call your supervisor to inform them of the situation.
- Don't forget to send your updated Incident report when all the details roll in.

Attached is the incident report template for your review.

records.title: Forcing a Full Sign-Out on a Departing Employee's Outlook Account
records.fullText:
Change the password to the email in GoDaddy.

Use Microsoft Edge and login to the email. Go to outlook.office365.com to login

Click the top right icon for your account. It should have initials and a circle around it.

Click View Account

Under the account name you will see the email address, and "why can't i edit" just below that click "Sign Out Everywhere"

This should sign you out. CALL the property and speak to the person who should have access to the account and confirm they DID get logged out. Make sure they don't just hit "log out" because what you are looking for is a FORCED logout on all devices.

**If you do not do this, the account holder will still have access to their email even if you change the password and remove devices. You HAVE to hit logout everywhere.**

records.file: slab/Support/Procedures/How to Upload Invoices in AppFolio.md
records.title: Uploading Invoices in AppFolio
records.fullText:
-Start by going into AppFolio - Accounting then Invoices

-Select the property you will be submitting an invoice to and the vendor

-Check to see if the invoice has already been submitted, if the invoice has not been submitted select the new invoice on the top left

-Input the Vendor and fill out the information.

-The expense type may be Capital or General

-Capital expense would be for the betterment of the property

-General expense would be for everything else

-The invoice number will be set up in the next format (Invoice Number). The property name will be the short one that is provided in the Line Items section.

-The invoice date will be the date on the invoice, while the accounting date may be the date that the invoice is uploaded into the system

-The section on the GL Account will be the number depending on the expense type and what kind of invoice it is.

-6XXX numbers will be General expense types

-8XXX numbers will be Capital expense types

-The unit price should be completed to be able to add taxes to the items

-The total amount needs to be the total amount including taxes

Adding Taxes

-When adding taxes, you need to check the boxes on the right side of 		each item.

-Once you have checked each box you go to Distribute

-Input the tax amount, check the taxable items box

-Then you click on OK

-Once the taxes have been added, the invoice documents need to be added

-Click on add and select the invoice file before uploading the document

-Once you have filled out everything with the * and have uploaded the document you can click on Save.
